definition_zh: 音乐的；悦耳的；有音乐天赋的；音乐剧
definition_en: connected with music, pleasant to hear like music, gifted at music, and also a stage show built from songs and dialogue
core_image: 舞台幕布升起，歌声与对白在同一束灯光里交替
scene: 排练厅的灯亮到深夜，演员们把同一段合唱重复了一遍又一遍。The cast rehearsed the new musical until the lights went out.
sceneCN: 这里是「音乐剧」（第 3 个义项：歌曲与对白交替推进的舞台作品）；句意为演员们排练这部新音乐剧，直到灯都灭了。

pos.zh: 音乐的；悦耳的；有音乐天赋的

collocations.zh: 音乐剧剧场；音乐剧艺术

derivatives.zh: 由 musical 加 -ly 构成，义为「在音乐上；悦耳地」
由 musical 加 -ity 构成，义为「音乐性；音乐感」
由 music 加 -ian 构成，指「音乐家」，与 musical 同出 music，并非由 musical 派生

senses.title: Connected with music as an art
senses.definition: belonging to music, or used in the making and study of music
senses.definitionCN: 属于音乐的，或用于创作与研究音乐的
senses.example: She has a musical ear and can pick out a tune after one hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一双音乐的耳朵，听一遍就能把曲调挑出来。
senses.why: The Latin suffix -alis turned musica into musicalis, meaning 'belonging to music', so this sense is the plain label the suffix was made for.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -alis 把 musica 变成 musicalis，意思就是「属于音乐的」，所以这个义项正是该后缀的本职。

senses.title: Pleasant to hear, as if sung
senses.definition: sounding sweet and rhythmical, the way a well-made melody sounds
senses.definitionCN: 听起来甜美而有节奏，像一段做得好的旋律
senses.example: Their voices blended into a musical murmur.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的嗓音融成一片悦耳的低语。
senses.why: A sound orderly enough to resemble music earns the same adjective, so the word moves from 'belonging to music' to 'sounding like music' and becomes praise.
senses.whyCN: 一种声音只要有序到近似音乐，就能用同一个形容词，于是词义从「属于音乐」滑到「像音乐一样好听」，变成一句称赞。

senses.title: A stage or screen work of songs and dialogue
senses.definition: a play or film in which songs and spoken scenes alternate, usually with dancing
senses.definitionCN: 歌曲与说白交替出现、通常还带舞蹈的舞台剧或影片
senses.example: The cast rehearsed the new musical until the lights went out.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们排练这部新音乐剧，直到灯都灭了。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century playbills shortened musical comedy to musical, and the adjective became a noun for an entire kind of show.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的戏单把 musical comedy 缩成 musical，这个形容词于是名词化，指一整类舞台作品。

senses.title: Gifted at music or sensitive to it
senses.definition: naturally aware of pitch and rhythm, or able to play and sing well
senses.definitionCN: 天生对音高与节奏敏感，或演奏演唱得好
senses.example: Even as a child he was unusually musical.
senses.exampleCN: 他小时候就显露出不寻常的音乐天赋。
senses.why: A person whose ear is tuned to music is described by the same adjective, so the word shifts from the art itself to the gift in the person.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵对音乐敏感的人也用这个形容词来描述，于是词义从艺术本身转到人身上的天赋。

intro.en: Musical is the adjective built on Latin musica with the suffix -alis; its noun use for a stage show came much later, from the theatre.
intro.cn: musical 是用后缀 -alis 加在拉丁语 musica 上构成的形容词；指舞台作品的名词用法要晚得多，来自剧院。

items.en: The Greek adjective mousikos described anything of the Muses, including a person trained in song and dance.
items.cn: 希腊语形容词 mousikos 形容一切属于缪斯的东西，也包括受过歌唱与舞蹈训练的人。

items.en: Latin kept musica for the art itself, the noun from which a whole set of adjectives could be built.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 musica 指这门艺术本身，这个名词后来又长出一整组形容词。

items.en: Musicalis added -alis to musica and meant simply 'relating to music', with no hint yet of the stage.
items.cn: musicalis 在 musica 后加 -alis，意思只是「与音乐有关的」，当时还没有舞台的含义。

items.en: Middle French passed musical to English, where it first described anything of music, from voices to instruments.
items.cn: 中古法语把 musical 传给英语，英语最初用它形容一切与音乐有关的东西，从嗓音到乐器。

items.en: In the nineteenth century musical was clipped from musical comedy and became a noun for a show of songs and spoken scenes.
items.cn: 十九世纪，musical 由 musical comedy 缩略而来，变成指「歌曲与说白并存的舞台作品」的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the adjective's own family and adverbs; the near-meaning group collects words for sounds that please the ear.
note.cn: 形近组收这个形容词的同族形式与副词；近义组收形容声音悦耳的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective is built on, naming the art of sound.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词所依附的名词，指声音的艺术。

entries.definition: The person noun from the same base, formed with -ian rather than -al.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的指人名词，用 -ian 而非 -al 构成。

entries.definition: The adverb built on musical with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musical 后加 -ly 构成的副词。

entries.definition: The noun built on musical with -ity, naming the quality of being musical.
entries.definitionCN: 在 musical 后加 -ity 构成的名词，指音乐性。

entries.definition: Relating to melody, or pleasant because of its melody.
entries.definitionCN: 与旋律有关的；因旋律而动听的。

entries.definition: Having a pleasant tune that is easy to hear and follow.
entries.definitionCN: 曲调优美、容易听清的。

entries.definition: Sweet-sounding, like a well-sung melody.
entries.definitionCN: 音调甜美的，像唱得好的旋律。

normalIntro.en: The adjective sits between the noun music and the person musician, and its suffixes show which one you mean.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词夹在名词 music 与指人的 musician 之间，后缀决定你指的是哪一边。

normal.en: The suffix -al turns the noun music into the adjective musical, just as nation becomes national.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 把名词 music 变成形容词 musical，就像 nation 变成 national 一样。

normal.en: The -al ending marks a quality, while -ian marks a person, which is the clean line between musical and musician.
normal.cn: -al 结尾标记性质，-ian 结尾标记人物，这就是 musical 与 musician 之间清楚的分界。

normal.en: The noun musical began as a short form of musical comedy on nineteenth-century playbills.
normal.cn: 名词 musical 起初是十九世纪戏单上 musical comedy 的缩略形式。

normal.en: A musical instrument is any instrument used for music, a fixed phrase that pins the adjective to its first sense.
normal.cn: a musical instrument 指任何用于音乐的乐器，这个固定搭配把形容词钉在第一个义项上。

normal.en: Musicality is musical plus -ity: the quality of having a musical ear, named as a noun.
normal.cn: musicality 是 musical 加 -ity，把「有音乐耳朵」这种性质变成名词。

abstract.en: One adjective describing a sound, a show and a person's ear shows how a single idea spreads over three very different things.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词既能形容声音、又能形容演出、还能形容人的耳朵，说明一个想法可以铺开到三种很不同的事物上。

abstract.en: When applause follows a song, the adjective quietly turns into a noun without changing a single letter.
abstract.cn: 歌声之后掌声响起，这个形容词便悄悄变成名词，一个字母都没改。

abstract.en: Calling a voice musical is a compliment that measures a human sound against an art form.
abstract.cn: 说一副嗓音 musical，是拿人的声音去比照一门艺术，本身就是称赞。

examples.en: The musical instruments were stored in a padded case.
examples.cn: 乐器被存放在一个带衬垫的箱子里。

examples.en: Her speaking voice is low and musical.
examples.cn: 她说话的声音低沉而悦耳。

examples.en: Tickets for the new musical sold out within a week.
examples.cn: 这部新音乐剧的门票一周内售罄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「缪齐扣」：缪斯一开口，歌声就扣住人；记住 musical 是音乐的、音乐剧。

root: 一般认为来自晚期拉丁语 musicalis（由 musica 加 -alis 构成），经中古法语 musical 进入英语；名词「音乐剧」是 musical comedy 的缩略。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts as a plain label for anything of music; it then stretches to sounds that please the ear, to a person's ear for music, and finally becomes a noun for a stage show.
sensesIntro.cn: 形容词最初只是「与音乐有关」的标签；随后扩展到悦耳的声音、人的音乐耳朵，最后名词化为一种舞台作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stage curtain rising on a song that carries the story forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台幕布升起，一首歌把故事往前推。

branches.en: a rehearsal room with a piano and a metronome
branches.cn: 摆着钢琴与节拍器的排练房

branches.en: a voice so smooth that the room goes quiet
branches.cn: 嗓音顺滑到让整个房间安静下来

branches.en: a child picking out a tune by ear
branches.cn: 孩子凭耳朵挑出一段曲调

branches.en: a curtain rising on dancers and singers
branches.cn: 幕布升起，舞者与歌者同台

branches.en: an audition settled by the quality of a voice
branches.cn: 由嗓音好坏决定结果的试演

intro.en: The adjective is music plus -al, and two further suffixes, -ly and -ity, turn it into an adverb and a quality noun.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是 music 加 -al，再加 -ly 与 -ity 两个后缀，就得到副词和表示性质的名词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin musicalis is the direct model: musica plus -alis, meaning simply belonging to music.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 musicalis 是直接的样板：musica 加 -alis，意思就是「属于音乐的」。

latinEntries.meaning: of music, and also a musician

definition_zh: 必须；一定；必需品
definition_en: used to say that something is necessary or almost certainly true; as a noun, something that cannot be left out
core_image: 一道关着的闸门，旁边只留一条必须走过去的通道
scene: 地铁入口处，安检员抬手示意乘客停下，把背包放上检查带。You must put your bag on the belt before you walk through.
sceneCN: 这里是「必须、有义务」（第 1 个义项：被要求做某事）；句意为过闸之前你得出示并放下背包接受检查。图中可辨识物件：闸门、检查带、背包。

collocations.zh: 一定做过（对过去的推测）

derivatives.zh: 由 must 与 have 复合，义为「必备品」
由 must 与 see 复合，义为「必看之物」

senses.title: To be obliged to do something
senses.definition: used to say that a person is obliged or forced to do something
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人有义务或不得不做某事
senses.example: You must show your ticket at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 你必须在门口出示车票。
senses.why: Old English moste was the past of motan and often meant had to; the old sense of permission narrowed into a demand, so the word now states an obligation rather than an option.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 moste 是 motan 的过去式，常表示「当时不得不」；原先的许可义收窄成强制义，所以这个词现在陈述的是义务，而不是选项。

senses.title: To be very likely true
senses.definition: used to say that something is almost certainly true, judging from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 依据证据判断某事几乎肯定成立
senses.example: The lights are off; they must have gone home.
senses.exampleCN: 灯都灭了，他们一定已经回家了。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be avoided, the mind treats the conclusion as unavoidable too, so the force of obligation slides into inference about what has to be the case.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事无法回避，人心也会把相应结论看成躲不开的，于是义务的力量滑向「情况必然如此」的推断。

senses.title: Something that cannot be left out
senses.definition: a thing that is absolutely necessary or strongly recommended
senses.definitionCN: 绝对必要或强烈建议不可省略的事物
senses.example: A torch is a must when you camp in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 在山里露营，手电是必备的。
senses.why: The noun keeps the force of the modal: anything called a must is treated as something one cannot skip, which is how a demand turns into an object on a packing list.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法保留了情态动词的力量：被称作 a must 的东西，被当成不能跳过的事物，于是一项要求就变成了清单上的一个物件。

intro.en: Must grew out of an Old English verb for being able or allowed; its past tense took over the present meaning of obligation.
intro.cn: must 源自古英语中表示「能够、被允许」的动词，它的过去式后来接管了现在时的义务义。

items.en: The verb reconstructed as motan is generally thought to have meant to have room or power to do something.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式 motan 意为「有做某事的余地或力量」。

items.en: Motan meant to be able or to be permitted, and its past tense moste often carried the practical sense of having to.
items.cn: motan 意为能够或被允许，其过去式 moste 常带有「只好、不得不」的实感。

items.en: Moste spread into more contexts than the old present form, and speakers began to use it for present obligations.
items.cn: moste 的使用范围超过了旧的现在式，说话人开始用它表达当下的义务。

items.en: Must settled as an unchanging present form, took a contracted negative mustn't, and lost the old infinitive and participle.
items.cn: must 固定为没有词形变化的现在式，出现缩略否定 mustn't，旧的动词不定式和分词形式逐渐消失。

items.en: Modern English adds the inference use and the countable noun a must, plus compounds such as must-have and must-see.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了推测用法和可数名词 a must，还产生 must-have、must-see 这类复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the negative contraction and three words that only resemble must in spelling; the near-meaning group holds other ways of expressing obligation.
note.cn: 形近组收 must 的否定缩略式，以及三个只是拼写相似、来源不同的词；近义组收其他表示义务的说法。

entries.definition: The contracted negative of must, common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: must 的否定缩略形式，口语中常见。

entries.definition: To gather people or courage for a purpose; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 召集人员或鼓起勇气；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A yellow sharp condiment made from seeds; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 用种子制成的黄色辛辣调味酱；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Smelling damp and stale, as an old room does; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 有潮湿霉味的；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Expresses external obligation like must, but uses do in questions and negatives.
entries.definitionCN: 与 must 一样表示外在义务，但疑问和否定要借助 do。

entries.definition: Gives advice or a mild duty rather than a firm demand.
entries.definitionCN: 给出建议或轻微责任，语气不如 must 强硬。

entries.definition: States a duty seen as right, often in careful or written English.
entries.definitionCN: 表示按道理应尽的责任，多见于正式或书面英语。

entries.definition: Names a requirement, usually followed by to before a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指出一项需求，动词前通常带 to。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic modal that drifted from permission to obligation, with a negative contraction and two modern compounds around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语情态动词，从许可漂移到义务，周围还有一个否定缩略式和两个现代复合词。

normal.en: Old English motan meant to be able or allowed, and its past moste meant had to; must is that past form grown into a present.
normal.cn: 古英语 motan 意为能够、被允许，其过去式 moste 意为不得不；must 就是这个过去式长成了现在式。

normal.en: Must is followed by the bare verb: must go, never must to go.
normal.cn: must 后面直接跟动词原形：说 must go，不说 must to go。

normal.en: Mustn't forbids, while can't denies a guess: you mustn't smoke here, but he can't be at home.
normal.cn: mustn't 表示禁止，can't 才用来否定推测：此处不许吸烟，而「他不可能在家」要用 can't。

normal.en: Must have done looks back at a past certainty, which is why the perfect follows must, not the past tense.
normal.cn: must have done 回看一件过去确定的事，所以 must 后面接完成式，而不是过去式。

normal.en: The noun a must copies the modal's force: a must-have item is one you cannot leave out.
normal.cn: 名词 a must 沿用了情态动词的力量：a must-have item 就是不能省略的东西。

abstract.en: A gate that only opens one way turns an old permission word into a word of compulsion.
abstract.cn: 一道只能单向打开的闸门，把旧的许可词变成了强制词。

abstract.en: When no other route exists, a demand and a certainty feel like the same pressure.
abstract.cn: 当没有别的路可走，一项要求和一种确定感会显得是同一种压力。

abstract.en: Every packing list is a small museum of things someone decided they could not do without.
abstract.cn: 每一张行李清单，都是「有人认定不能没有」的小小陈列馆。

examples.en: Visitors must sign in at the front desk.
examples.cn: 访客必须在前台登记。

examples.en: She must have missed the last bus.
examples.cn: 她一定是错过了末班车。

examples.en: A good pair of gloves is a must in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天一副好手套是必备的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马斯特」——教练马斯特站在跑道边说：必须跑完这一圈；must 就是必须。

root: 古英语 motan（能够、被允许），过去式 moste 逐渐固定为 must；一般认为与德语 müssen 同出原始日耳曼语 motan，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an unavoidable demand; from it grow the inference about what must be true and the noun for a thing one cannot leave out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是躲不开的要求；由此长出「情况必然如此」的推断，以及指「不能省略之物」的名词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate with only one open passage, where stopping is not an option.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道只留一条通道的闸门，停下不在选项之内。

branches.en: a guard raising a hand at the entrance
branches.cn: 入口处抬手示意的安检员

branches.en: a bag opened before the belt
branches.cn: 放上检查带之前的背包

branches.en: a dark window and a guess about who is inside
branches.cn: 暗着的窗和关于里面是谁的猜测

branches.en: a note that reads had to, written as must
branches.cn: 把「不得不」写成 must 的便条

branches.en: a torch placed first in the camp bag
branches.cn: 露营包里最先放手电的位置

intro.en: The word rests on one Old English modal, its past form, a negative clitic, and two modern compounds that turn the modal into a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的一个情态动词、它的过去式、一个否定附着成分，以及两个把情态动词变成名词的现代复合词支撑。

latinIntro.en: Must belongs to the Germanic modals, so no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: must 属于日耳曼语情态动词，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

was able, was allowed, had to

definition_zh: 我的；用于感叹或称呼
definition_en: belonging to the speaker; also used in exclamations and in polite forms of address
core_image: 一只手把一件东西按在自己胸前，表示这件东西归我
scene: 门口的木架上挂着两件外套，一件深蓝，一件灰色。My coat is the blue one hanging by the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「我的」（第 1 个义项：表示所属）；句意为挂在门边的那件蓝色外套是我的。图中可辨识物件：木架、两件外套、门。

pos.zh: 我的（形容词性物主代词）

derivatives.zh: my 的名词性形式，后面不接名词，义为「我的（东西）」
my 与 self 结合而成的反身代词，义为「我自己」

senses.title: Belonging to the speaker
senses.definition: belonging to the person who is speaking, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 属于说话人，用在名词之前
senses.example: My coat is the blue one hanging by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 挂在门边的那件蓝色外套是我的。
senses.why: Old English min was the genitive of the first person; a shortened form took over before nouns, so the word now points at an owner rather than naming a person.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 min 是第一人称的属格形式；一个缩短的形式在名词前占了上风，于是这个词现在指向所有者，而不是称呼某个人。

senses.title: Used in exclamations
senses.definition: used at the start of an exclamation to show surprise or dismay
senses.definitionCN: 放在感叹句开头，表示惊讶或不安
senses.example: My goodness, that was a close call.
senses.exampleCN: 天哪，刚才真是好险。
senses.why: The owner word became a way to put the speaker at the centre of a reaction, so my goodness means the surprise belongs to me, not to the thing seen.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示所有者的词变成了把说话人放在反应中心的手段，所以 my goodness 意味着惊讶属于我，而不是属于看到的东西。

senses.title: Used in polite address
senses.titleCN: 用于称呼（如亲爱的、大人）
senses.definition: used before a title or a term of address in courteous or old-fashioned speech
senses.definitionCN: 用于礼貌或老派的称呼之前
senses.example: My dear friend, you have nothing to worry about.
senses.exampleCN: 亲爱的朋友，你没有什么可担心的。
senses.why: A speaker who calls someone my dear marks that person as belonging to his circle of care, which is why the owner word turned into a marker of warmth.
senses.whyCN: 说话人叫对方 my dear，是把对方划进自己关心的圈子，这个表所属的词因此变成了表示亲切的标记。

intro.en: My is the genitive of the English first person, shortened from an Old English form that also produced mine.
intro.cn: my 是英语第一人称的属格形式，由古英语的一个形式缩短而来，mine 也出自同一来源。

items.en: A first person stem reconstructed with the shape me- is generally taken as the source of the possessive forms across the family.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构为 me- 的第一人称词干是整个语族中各种所有格形式的来源。

items.en: The possessive was reconstructed as minaz, marked for the speaker and agreeing with the thing owned.
items.cn: 所有格被重构为 minaz，既标记说话人，也随被拥有之物变化。

items.en: Old English used min before nouns and as a standalone form, with different endings for gender and number.
items.cn: 古英语用 min 放在名词前，也可单独使用，并随性与数变化词尾。

items.en: Middle English shortened min to mi before consonants and kept mine before vowels, a pattern still visible in the modern pair.
items.cn: 中古英语在辅音前把 min 缩成 mi，在元音前保留 mine，这一分别仍留在现代的一对形式里。

items.en: Modern English fixed my before nouns and mine on its own, and the two stopped differing by the following sound.
items.cn: 现代英语固定为名词前用 my、单独用 mine，两者不再随后面音素区分。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the nominal possessive and the reflexive built on the same stem, plus one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group collects other possessives.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的名词性所有格与反身代词，另加一个只是外形相似的词；近义组收其他所有格形式。

entries.definition: The possessive used without a following noun.
entries.definitionCN: 后面不接名词的名词性所有格，义为「我的」。

entries.definition: The object form of the first person singular.
entries.definitionCN: 第一人称单数的宾格形式。

entries.definition: The reflexive pronoun built from the same possessive stem.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一所有格词干构成的反身代词。

entries.definition: Short sight, from a Greek word for squinting; only the opening looks alike.
entries.definitionCN: 近视，源自希腊语「眯眼」；只是开头拼写相似，词源不同。

entries.definition: Belonging to the speaker together with others.
entries.definitionCN: 属于说话人以及其他人；我们的。

entries.definition: Belonging to the person spoken to.
entries.definitionCN: 属于听话的人；你的。

entries.definition: Belonging to people or things already mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 属于已提到的人或物；他们的。

entries.definition: Belonging to a male person already mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 属于已提到的男性；他的。

normalIntro.en: The word is the short form of an Old English possessive, and its longer relative survives as mine and inside myself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古英语所有格的缩短形式，较长的形态仍以 mine 以及 myself 的组成部分存活。

normal.en: Old English min became mi before consonants and my in modern spelling, so my and mine are two shapes of one word.
normal.cn: 古英语 min 在辅音前变成 mi，后来写作 my，所以 my 与 mine 是同一个词的两个形态。

normal.en: My must stand before a noun; standing alone it becomes mine: my book, but the book is mine.
normal.cn: my 必须放在名词前；单独使用要变 mine：说 my book，但说 the book is mine。

normal.en: My takes no plural and no gender; unlike Latin meus, it never changes for the thing owned.
normal.cn: my 没有复数，也不分性别；不像拉丁语 meus，它从不随被拥有之物变形。

normal.en: My goodness and my word are fixed exclamations, not statements about owning anything.
normal.cn: my goodness 与 my word 是固定的感叹语，不是在陈述拥有什么。

normal.en: In my dear and my lord the word marks closeness or rank, a use that goes back to forms of address.
normal.cn: 在 my dear 与 my lord 里，这个词标记亲近或身份，这种用法来自称呼语。

abstract.en: A hand pressed to the chest says ownership is measured from the speaker outward.
abstract.cn: 一只手按在胸前，说明「所有」是从说话人向外量出来的。

abstract.en: A single letter added to a name turns a person into a position in someone else's life.
abstract.cn: 一个称呼前加上这个词，就把一个人变成了另一个人生活里的位置。

abstract.en: English possessives are short because the speaker is never far from what is claimed.
abstract.cn: 英语的所有格都很短，因为说话人离自己所声称的东西从来不远。

examples.en: My notes are on the kitchen table.
examples.cn: 我的笔记在厨房桌上。

examples.en: My grandmother taught me to sew.
examples.cn: 我外婆教我缝纫。

examples.en: I have lost my keys again.
examples.cn: 我又把钥匙弄丢了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买」——my 读音近「买」，我的东西都是我买的。

root: 古英语 min（我的，第一人称属格）缩短为 my；与拉丁语 meus、希腊语词干 me- 同出原始印欧语第一人称词干。

sensesIntro.en: The core is ownership anchored in the speaker; the other senses stretch that anchor into exclamations and forms of address.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「以说话人为锚点的所有」；其余义项把这个锚点伸向感叹语与称呼语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing an object to the chest, marking it as mine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把物件按在胸前，标记它归我。

branches.en: a blue coat claimed at the door
branches.cn: 在门口被认领的蓝色外套

branches.en: a name written on a school bag
branches.cn: 写在书包上的名字

branches.en: hands raised at a near miss
branches.cn: 险些出事时抬起的手

branches.en: a breath let out after a shock
branches.cn: 受惊之后呼出的一口气

branches.en: a greeting spoken to an old friend
branches.cn: 对老朋友说出的问候

intro.en: The word is one short English form of a possessive stem that also yields the standalone form and the reflexive.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语所有格词干的一个短形态，同一词干还产出单独使用的形式和反身代词。

latinIntro.en: Latin carries the same first person stem in its possessive, which inflects for gender where English my does not.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的所有格带着同一个第一人称词干，并且随性别变化，而英语的 my 不变。

definition_zh: 我自己；我本人；独自
definition_en: the reflexive pronoun for the speaker, used when the speaker is the object, for emphasis, or in the phrase by myself meaning alone
core_image: 镜子里的人抬手，镜外的手也同时抬起，两边是同一个人
scene: 厨房里，砧板和菜刀摆在水池边，洋葱刚切到一半。I cut myself while chopping onions for dinner.
sceneCN: 这里是「我自己」（第 1 个义项：反身用法，动作回到主语本身）；句意为切洋葱做晚饭时我割伤了自己。图中可辨识物件：砧板、菜刀、洋葱。

derivatives.zh: myself 中的 self 部分，义为「自身、自我」
由 self 加 -ish 构成，义为「自私的」
由 self 加 -less 构成，义为「无私的」

senses.title: The speaker as the object of his own action
senses.definition: used as the object when the subject and the object are the same speaker
senses.definitionCN: 主语和宾语是同一个人（说话人）时用作宾语
senses.example: I cut myself while chopping onions for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 切洋葱做晚饭时我割伤了自己。
senses.why: English marks a returning action with a compound of the owner word and self, so the doer appears a second time inside the sentence as the one acted on.
senses.whyCN: 英语用「所有者词加 self」的复合形式标记回到自身的动作，于是动作发出者在句中第二次出现，成了被作用的人。

senses.title: The speaker, emphasized
senses.definition: used after a noun or at the end of a clause to stress that it was the speaker and no one else
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词后或句末，强调是说话人本人而不是别人
senses.example: I built these shelves myself.
senses.exampleCN: 这些架子是我自己搭的。
senses.why: The same compound can stand outside the verb's arguments and simply point at the speaker, which turns a reflexive into a spotlight.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复合形式可以站在动词论元之外，单纯指向说话人，于是反身代词变成了一束追光。

senses.title: Alone, without company
senses.definition: used with by to say that the speaker is without other people
senses.definitionCN: 与 by 连用，表示身边没有别人
senses.example: I went to the cinema by myself.
senses.exampleCN: 我一个人去看了电影。
senses.why: If the speaker is the only one present, the returning self has no one else to lean on, so the reflexive phrase comes to mean solitude.
senses.whyCN: 如果只有说话人在场，那个回到自身的「我」没有别人可以依靠，反身短语于是引申出「独处」的意思。

intro.en: Myself joins the English possessive my to self, a Germanic word for one's own person that Old English already used in reflexive compounds.
intro.cn: myself 把英语所有格 my 与 self 结合；self 是日耳曼语中表示「自身」的词，古英语已用它构成反身复合形式。

items.en: A stem reconstructed as selbho- is often proposed for the reflexive family, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 常有人为这一族反身词提出重构形式 selbho-，但该重构并不确定。

items.en: The adjective selbaz meant the same person or the very one, and it supplied the base for self.
items.cn: 形容词 selbaz 意为「同一个人、正是那个人」，为 self 提供了基础。

items.en: Old English seolf or self could stand alone as a pronoun and appear in compounds with possessive forms.
items.cn: 古英语 seolf 或 self 可单独作代词，也能与所有格形式组合。

items.en: Middle English wrote combinations such as mi self as two words, and the pattern spread to every person of the pronoun.
items.cn: 中古英语把 mi self 这类组合写成两个词，这一模式扩展到人称代词的每一人称。

items.en: Modern English fused the parts into myself, added the emphatic and the by-phrase uses, and kept the plural pattern ourselves.
items.cn: 现代英语把两部分合并为 myself，发展出强调用法和 by 短语用法，并保留了复数形式 ourselves。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the parallel reflexives for other persons; the near-meaning group holds the bare pronouns and the idea of being alone.
note.cn: 形近组收其他人称的平行反身代词；近义组收不带 self 的代词以及「独自一人」这层意思。

entries.definition: The reflexive for the person spoken to, built the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 听话人的反身代词，构造方式相同。

entries.definition: The reflexive for a male third person.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称男性的反身代词。

entries.definition: The reflexive for we, with the plural selves.
entries.definitionCN: we 的反身代词，用复数形式 selves。

entries.definition: The reflexive for it, used for things and animals.
entries.definitionCN: it 的反身代词，用于事物和动物。

entries.definition: The plain object pronoun, used where the action does not return.
entries.definitionCN: 普通的宾格代词，动作不回到自身时使用。

entries.definition: The subject pronoun that myself points back to.
entries.definitionCN: 主格代词，myself 所指回的对象。

entries.definition: The general reflexive for an unspecified person.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某人的反身代词。

entries.definition: Without other people present, the sense carried by by myself.
entries.definitionCN: 身边没有别人，即 by myself 所表达的意思。

normalIntro.en: The word is my plus self, and the same recipe is repeated across the whole pronoun system.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 my 加 self，同一配方在人称代词的整套系统里反复使用。

normal.en: My plus self gives myself; the plural keeps the same recipe and changes my to our: ourselves.
normal.cn: my 加 self 得到 myself；复数沿用同一配方，把 my 换成 our，得到 ourselves。

normal.en: When the subject and the object are the same person, English uses the self form: I hurt myself, not I hurt me.
normal.cn: 主语和宾语是同一个人时，英语用带 self 的形式：说 I hurt myself，不说 I hurt me。

normal.en: Myself cannot be the subject of a finite verb; emphasis uses I myself or a final myself instead.
normal.cn: myself 不能充当限定动词的主语；要强调可以用 I myself，或把 myself 放在句末。

normal.en: By myself means alone; beside myself means out of control, not standing next to the body.
normal.cn: by myself 意为独自；beside myself 意为情绪失控，而不是站在身体旁边。

normal.en: In including myself, the self form works after a preposition or at the end of a list.
normal.cn: 在 including myself 里，这个反身形式用在介词后或列表末尾。

abstract.en: A mirror is the plainest picture of a sentence that turns back on its speaker.
abstract.cn: 镜子是一个句子折回说话人时最直白的画面。

abstract.en: A spotlight aimed at one person explains the emphatic use better than any rule.
abstract.cn: 一束只照一个人的追光，比任何规则都更能解释强调用法。

abstract.en: An empty cinema seat makes the meaning of by myself visible at once.
abstract.cn: 一个空着的电影院座位，一眼就能让人看见 by myself 的含义。

examples.en: I taught myself to play the guitar.
examples.cn: 我自学弹吉他。

examples.en: I painted the whole fence myself.
examples.cn: 整道栅栏都是我自己刷的。

examples.en: I waited by myself for over an hour.
examples.cn: 我独自等了一个多小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买赛尔夫」——自己给自己买东西，就叫 myself，我自己。

root: my 与古英语 self（自身）复合而成；self 一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 selbaz，拉丁语 ipse 只是意义相近，并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the speaker turning back on the speaker; emphasis and solitude are two ways that turn becomes visible.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是说话人把动作折回自己；强调用法与独处义，是这一折返的两种显形方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised before a mirror, with the reflected hand rising at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜前抬起一只手，镜中的手在同一刻也抬起。

branches.en: a cut finger held under the tap
branches.cn: 在水龙头下按住割伤的手指

branches.en: a sentence whose object is its subject
branches.cn: 宾语与主语是同一个人的句子

branches.en: a shelf built without help
branches.cn: 没有帮手也照样搭好的架子

branches.en: a ticket bought for one seat only
branches.cn: 只买了一个座位的票

branches.en: an empty row in a dark cinema
branches.cn: 黑暗影院里空着的一排座位

intro.en: The word is a compound of the possessive my and the Germanic self, and the same pieces recur in every reflexive pronoun.
intro.cn: 这个词由所有格 my 与日耳曼语的 self 复合而成，同样的部件在每个人称的反身代词中都会重现。

latinIntro.en: Latin has a reflexive pronoun of its own, but no form of it is a reliable source for self, so the cognate list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语有自己的反身代词，但其中没有任何形式可以可靠地作为 self 的来源，因此同源词列表留空。

items.meaning: the speaker as object or emphasis

definition_zh: 谜；神秘事物；神秘气氛；悬疑作品
definition_en: something that cannot be explained or is kept secret; the quality of being secret; a story built around an unsolved puzzle
core_image: 一只上锁的抽屉，里面的东西不翼而飞，锁却完好无损
scene: 书房的抽屉少了一封信，锁面没有撬痕，窗子也从里面扣着。The letter vanished from a locked drawer, and the mystery is still unsolved.
sceneCN: 这里是「谜、无法解释的事」（第 1 个义项：找不到答案的事件）；句意为信从上锁的抽屉里消失，这个谜至今未解。图中可辨识物件：抽屉、锁、信、窗扣。

pos.zh: 谜；神秘事物；神秘气氛；悬疑作品

derivatives.zh: 由 mystery 的词干加 -ous 构成，义为「神秘的」
由 mysterious 加 -ly 构成，义为「神秘地」
由同一词干加 -ify 构成，义为「使困惑不解」
由 mystic 加 -ism 构成，义为「神秘主义」

senses.title: Something that cannot be explained
senses.definition: a fact or event that resists explanation and keeps people guessing
senses.definitionCN: 无法解释、让人不断猜测的事实或事件
senses.example: The letter vanished from a locked drawer, and the mystery is still unsolved.
senses.exampleCN: 信从上锁的抽屉里消失，这个谜至今未解。
senses.why: The Greek noun named rites closed to outsiders; once the ritual frame fell away, what remained was a fact shut off from explanation, which is the everyday sense today.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词本指不许外人参加的仪式；仪式的外壳脱落之后，剩下的就是一个被挡在解释之外的事实，也就是今天的日常义。

senses.title: The quality of being secret or strange
senses.definition: an atmosphere of secrecy that surrounds a person, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 笼罩在人、地点或事物周围的神秘气息
senses.example: An air of mystery hangs over the house at the end of the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 巷子尽头那座房子笼罩着一层神秘气息。
senses.why: Because the word names what is withheld, it can also name the withheld quality itself, so a place becomes mysterious by carrying a mystery rather than by containing one.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词指被扣住不说的东西，它也能指那种被扣住的性质本身，于是一个地方不必真的藏着什么谜，只要带着谜的气息就显得神秘。

senses.title: A story built around a puzzle
senses.definition: a book, film or play whose plot turns on an unexplained event and its solution
senses.definitionCN: 以未解事件及其解答为主线的小说、电影或戏剧
senses.example: She reads a murder mystery every week before bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周睡前读一本谋杀悬疑小说。
senses.why: Readers wanted the pleasure of a puzzle that gets solved, so the word moved from the puzzle itself to the kind of book that delivers one.
senses.whyCN: 读者想要的是「谜被解开」的快感，于是这个词从谜本身转到了提供这种谜的那类书。

intro.en: Mystery reached English through Old French from Latin, and the Latin noun had already borrowed a Greek word for rites open only to the initiated.
intro.cn: mystery 经古法语、拉丁语进入英语，而拉丁语名词此前已借入一个希腊词，指只许入会者参加的仪式。

items.en: The verb myein meant to close, especially the lips or the eyes, and the sense of shutting away runs through the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 myein 意为闭合，尤指闭嘴或闭眼，这一族词始终带着「关起来」的意思。

items.en: A mysterion was a secret rite or teaching that insiders guarded from outsiders.
items.cn: mysterion 指内部人对外人守口如瓶的秘密仪式或教义。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as mysterium, where the sense widened from a rite to any hidden matter.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 mysterium，词义从仪式扩大到任何隐秘之事。

items.en: Old French mistere carried both the religious sense and the sense of a hidden truth, and passed the word to English.
items.cn: 古法语 mistere 兼有宗教义与「隐秘真相」义，并把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the puzzle sense, adds the atmosphere sense and the name of a literary genre.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「谜」义，又添上「气氛」义，并把词用作一类文学体裁的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective, the verb and other relatives on the same stem; the near-meaning group holds words for puzzles and secrets.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形容词、动词及其他同族词；近义组收表示谜题与秘密的词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing what cannot be explained.
entries.definitionCN: 形容无法解释之事的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb for something done in an unexplained way.
entries.definitionCN: 表示以难以解释的方式。

entries.definition: To baffle someone, as if by a closed door.
entries.definitionCN: 使人困惑，仿佛面对一扇关着的门。

entries.definition: The belief that the divine can be reached directly.
entries.definitionCN: 认为可以直接抵达神性的信仰。

entries.definition: A traditional story about gods or origins; the similarity is only in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 关于神或起源的传统故事；只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A problem that needs thought before it can be solved.
entries.definitionCN: 需要思考才能解决的问题。

entries.definition: A fact kept from others on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 有意不让他人知道的事实。

entries.definition: A question or object whose meaning is deliberately hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 含义被有意藏起来的提问或物件。

entries.definition: A person or thing that is impossible to read.
entries.definitionCN: 无法看透的人或事物。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a name for closed rites and now covers any unexplained fact, the feeling around it, and the books written about it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是闭门仪式的名称，如今覆盖任何无法解释的事实、围绕它的感觉，以及以此为题材的书。

normal.en: The word goes back to Greek myein, to close the lips; a mystery is something someone keeps their mouth shut about.
normal.cn: 这个词可追到希腊语 myein（闭嘴）；mystery 就是有人闭口不谈的事。

normal.en: The plural is mysteries, with y changing to ies, the same pattern as story and stories.
normal.cn: 复数是 mysteries，y 变 ies，与 story、stories 的变化方式相同。

normal.en: Mystery is the noun, mysterious the adjective, mystify the verb; the family keeps one stem and changes only the ending.
normal.cn: mystery 是名词，mysterious 是形容词，mystify 是动词；这一族共用同一词干，只换词尾。

normal.en: An air of mystery needs no hidden fact; it can be produced by a closed door and a dim lamp.
normal.cn: an air of mystery 并不需要真藏着什么；一扇关着的门和一盏昏暗的灯就能造出它。

normal.en: A murder mystery is a genre label, so the word can name a shelf in a bookshop as well as a puzzle in a locked room.
normal.cn: a murder mystery 是体裁标签，所以这个词既能指密室里的谜，也能指书店里的一个书架。

abstract.en: A locked drawer with nothing missing teaches that a question can outlast its answer.
abstract.cn: 一只什么都没丢的上锁抽屉，说明问题可以比答案活得更久。

abstract.en: Every secret is a room whose door is shut from the inside, and every mystery is the light under that door.
abstract.cn: 每个秘密都是从里面关上的房间，而每个谜都是门缝下透出的光。

abstract.en: A word that names a closed rite ends up naming the pleasure of watching a lock be picked.
abstract.cn: 一个命名闭门仪式的词，最后用来命名「看别人开锁」的乐趣。

examples.en: The cause of the fire remains a mystery.
examples.cn: 起火的原因仍然是个谜。

examples.en: He enjoys solving mysteries set in old hotels.
examples.cn: 他喜欢破解以老旅馆为背景的谜案。

examples.en: Her sudden departure is shrouded in mystery.
examples.cn: 她的突然离开笼罩在神秘之中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯特瑞」——秘密被锁在密室里，就成了谜；mystery 就是谜。

root: 希腊语 myein（闭口、闭眼）派生的 mysterion（秘仪）经拉丁语 mysterium、古法语 mistere 进入英语；一般认为核心是「对外人闭合」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fact kept behind a closed door; the senses extend to the atmosphere such a fact creates and to stories built on solving it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被关在门后的事实；义项扩展到这种事实造成的气氛，以及以解开它为骨架的故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked drawer standing open with its contents gone and its lock unbroken.
core.cn: 核心意象：锁完好无损，抽屉却开着，里面的东西不见了。

branches.en: a letter missing from a locked drawer
branches.cn: 上锁抽屉里不见了的信

branches.en: a detective holding a key that fits nothing
branches.cn: 拿着一把配不上任何锁的钥匙的侦探

branches.en: a dim lamp behind drawn curtains
branches.cn: 拉上窗帘后的一盏暗灯

branches.en: a house no neighbour will talk about
branches.cn: 邻居都不愿提起的房子

branches.en: a paperback left open at the last page
branches.cn: 摊在最后一页的平装书

intro.en: The word passes from a Greek verb of closing through a Greek noun, a Latin borrowing and an Old French form before it names a puzzle in English.
intro.cn: 这个词从希腊语表「闭合」的动词出发，经希腊名词、拉丁借形与古法语形式，最后在英语里指一个谜。

latinIntro.en: Latin carried the Greek noun into mysterium and also used the plural mysteria for the rites themselves.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词带入 mysterium，也用复数 mysteria 指仪式本身。

items.meaning: to close the lips or eyes

definition_zh: 指甲；趾甲；钉子；钉住；逮住
definition_en: the hard plate at the end of a finger or toe; a small metal pin used to fasten things; and, as a verb, to fix something with such a pin or to catch someone
core_image: 锤子落下，一枚小钉被送进木板，只留下一个扁平的钉帽
scene: 修鞋摊的木板上钉着一排旧鞋掌，师傅抬手示意我别碰那块松动的边角。He drove a nail into the loose board so that it would stop rattling.
sceneCN: 这里是「钉子」（第 2 个义项：用来连接或固定木料的金属小钉）；句意是他把一枚钉子钉进松动的木板，好让它不再吱呀作响。图中可辨识物件：钉帽、旧鞋掌、木凳。

collocations.phrase: hit the nail on the head

derivatives.zh: 由 finger 与 nail 复合而成，义为「手指甲」
由 toe 与 nail 复合而成，义为「脚趾甲」
由 nail 与 brush 复合而成，义为「指甲刷」

senses.title: The hard plate at the end of a finger or toe
senses.definition: the hard, smooth layer that grows at the end of a finger or toe and protects the tip
senses.definitionCN: 手指或脚趾末端长出的坚硬平滑层，用来保护指端
senses.example: She kept her nails short so that she could work at the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 为了能在机器旁干活，她把指甲一直剪得很短。
senses.why: Old English nægl named this hard plate first; the metal pin took the same word because both are small, hard and gripping.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nægl 最早指的就是这层硬片；金属钉后来共用同一个词，因为两者都是又小又硬、能把东西咬住的东西。

senses.title: A small metal pin used for fastening
senses.definition: a short metal spike driven into wood or a wall to join pieces or hold something in place
senses.definitionCN: 钉入木头或墙面的短金属钉，用来连接构件或把东西固定住
senses.example: The picture hung from a single nail above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅画就挂在门上方的一枚钉子上。
senses.why: The Germanic word covered both the body's hard plate and the metal peg, so the shared picture is a small hard thing that holds on.
senses.whyCN: 这个日耳曼词同时指身体的硬片和金属小钉，共有的画面就是一件小而硬、能牢牢咬住的东西。

senses.title: To fasten something with a nail
senses.definition: to fix an object in place by driving a nail into it, or to attach one thing to another in this way
senses.definitionCN: 把钉子钉入某物使其固定，或以这种方式把两件东西连接起来
senses.example: They nailed boards over the broken window before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，他们用木板钉住了破掉的窗户。
senses.why: Once the noun names the tool, the verb needs no new idea: it simply names the act of putting that tool to work.
senses.whyCN: 名词既已指这件工具，动词就不需要新意思，只是把「使用这件工具」的动作说出来。

senses.title: To catch or hit exactly
senses.definition: in informal speech, to catch someone, to hit something exactly, or to do something perfectly
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示抓住某人、正好击中某物，或把事情办得无可挑剔
senses.example: The police nailed the driver at the second checkpoint.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在第二个检查站逮住了那个司机。
senses.why: A nail stops a board from moving, so the verb can picture anything pinned down beyond doubt: a suspect caught, a target hit, an answer found.
senses.whyCN: 钉子能止住木板的活动，所以这个动词可以想像任何被钉死、再无疑问的事：抓到嫌疑人、击中目标、找到答案。

intro.en: Nail is a Germanic word that has named both a hard plate on the body and a metal pin since Old English, and the two senses still share one form.
intro.cn: nail 是日耳曼语词，自古英语起就同时指身上的硬片和金属钉，这两个义项至今共用一个词形。

items.en: A reconstructed root for nail or claw is generally linked to this word, though the exact shape of the root is disputed.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词与一个表示「指甲、爪」的原始印欧语词根有关，但词根的具体形式仍有争议。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form naglaz named both the hard plate of a finger or toe and a metal peg.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式 naglaz 同时指手指或脚趾的硬片与金属钉。

items.en: Old English nægl carried both meanings, so a finger nail and a board nail were the same word from the start.
items.cn: 古英语 nægl 兼具两义，所以手指甲和木板钉从一开始就是同一个词。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun and formed the verb nailen, meaning to fasten with a nail.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个名词，并造出动词 nailen，意为用钉子固定。

items.en: Modern English adds the informal sense of catching someone or getting something exactly right, as in nailing a suspect or an answer.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了口语义：抓住某人或把事情做得丝毫不差，如 nail a suspect、nail an answer。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely sound or look close to nail; the near-meaning group collects words for claws, pins and the act of fastening.
note.cn: 形近组收只是读音或拼写接近 nail 的词；近义组收表示爪、钉以及固定动作的词。

entries.definition: A small soft creature that moves slowly with a shell on its back; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 背壳、行动缓慢的小软体动物；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The small hollow in the middle of the stomach; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 腹部中间的凹陷，即肚脐；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The back of the neck; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 后颈；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The nail on a finger, formed from finger and nail.
entries.definitionCN: 手指上的指甲，由 finger 与 nail 复合而成。

entries.definition: A sharp curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟类或动物脚上弯曲而锋利的爪。

entries.definition: A short thin piece of metal used to hold things together.
entries.definitionCN: 用来把东西固定在一起的短细金属件。

entries.definition: To attach or fix something firmly in place.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定或连接在某处。

entries.definition: A small short nail with a wide head, used for cloth or paper.
entries.definitionCN: 钉布或纸用的、钉帽较宽的小短钉。

normalIntro.en: The word has been one shape for two jobs since Old English, and every sense grows out of something small and hard that holds.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词自古英语起就用一个词形承担两件事，每个义项都从「小而硬、能咬住」这个画面长出来。

normal.en: Old English nægl meant both finger nail and metal nail, so the two senses are twins rather than one borrowed from the other.
normal.cn: 古英语 nægl 同时指指甲和金属钉，两义是双胞胎，并非一个从另一个借来。

normal.en: Nailing a board is the verb built straight from the noun, which is why it needs no separate history.
normal.cn: 钉木板这个动词直接由名词构成，所以它没有另一段词源。

normal.en: Fingernail and toenail are compounds of finger or toe with nail, and each keeps the body sense.
normal.cn: fingernail 与 toenail 分别是 finger、toe 与 nail 的复合词，都保留了身体义。

normal.en: Hit the nail on the head pictures a hammer striking the exact spot, so the phrase means getting it exactly right.
normal.cn: 「hit the nail on the head」想像锤子正落在钉头上，所以这个说法指说得丝毫不差。

normal.en: Nail down adds down: the nail is driven fully home, so the details are fixed and no longer move.
normal.cn: nail down 加了 down：钉子被彻底钉到底，于是细节定死，不再变动。

abstract.en: A nail is a tiny thing that decides whether a heavy board stays put, which is why the word also means certainty.
abstract.cn: 钉子虽小，却决定一块重木板是否稳住，所以这个词也带有「确定」的意味。

abstract.en: Finger nail and metal nail share one word because both are a hard edge at the boundary of something softer.
abstract.cn: 指甲与铁钉共用一个词，因为两者都是较软之物边界上的一层硬边。

abstract.en: When police nail a suspect, the image is a case pinned down so that it can no longer shift.
abstract.cn: 警察 nail 住嫌疑人时，画面是一个案子被钉死，再也不能松动。

examples.en: He drove a nail into the loose board so that it would stop rattling.
examples.cn: 他把一枚钉子钉进松动的木板，好让它不再吱呀作响。

examples.en: She painted her nails a pale pink before the interview.
examples.cn: 面试前她把指甲涂成了淡粉色。

examples.en: The police nailed the driver at the second checkpoint.
examples.cn: 警方在第二个检查站逮住了那个司机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「耐哦」——钉子钉进去很耐，指甲也耐磨；记住 nail 是指甲、钉子，也是钉住。

root: 古英语 nægl（指甲；钉子），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 naglaz，更早或与原始印欧语表示「指甲、爪」的词根有关；同族词有 fingernail、toenail、nailbrush 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small hard plate or peg; the senses then divide into the body part, the metal tool, the act of using it, and the informal idea of pinning something down for certain.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一小片硬物或小钉；义项分出身体部位、金属工具、使用工具的动作，以及口语中「把某事钉死、再也无法狡辩」的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hammer drives a small hard pin into wood until only its flat head shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：锤子把小硬钉送进木板，最后只剩一个扁平的钉帽露在外面。

branches.en: a hand resting on a table, the tip of each finger capped in hard plate
branches.cn: 一只手搭在桌上，每个指尖都覆着一层硬片

branches.en: a row of clipped nails left on the edge of a basin
branches.cn: 脸盆边留下一排剪下的指甲

branches.en: one nail holding a heavy picture against a wall
branches.cn: 一枚钉子把沉重的画固定在墙上

branches.en: a hammer swinging down and a board going still
branches.cn: 锤子落下，木板随即不再晃动

branches.en: a case closed because the last doubt has been pinned down
branches.cn: 最后一个疑点被钉死，案子随之了结

intro.en: The entry is held together by one Old English noun, its English verb, and the compounds and endings built on it.
intro.cn: 这个词条由一个古英语名词、由它而来的英语动词，以及建在它上面的复合词与词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, and Latin has no noun that English used to build it, so no Latin cognate is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族，拉丁语中没有英语用来构词的对应名词，所以这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: nail of a finger or toe, metal peg
hard plate or small metal pin

definition_zh: 裸体的；赤裸的；无遮盖的；不加掩饰的
definition_en: not wearing any clothes; not covered by the usual layer; or stated openly without disguise
core_image: 层层遮盖被一层层剥去，最后只剩没有任何外物包裹的身体
scene: 清晨的海滩上空无一人，几个孩子把衣服堆在沙丘边，光着脚往浪里跑。The boy ran naked into the cold water and came back laughing.
sceneCN: 这里是「裸体的、没穿衣服的」（第 1 个义项：身上没有任何衣物）；句意是男孩光着身子跑进冷水里，又笑着跑回来。图中可辨识物件：沙丘边的衣服、浅浪、光脚。

pos.zh: 裸体的；无遮盖的；不加掩饰的

derivatives.zh: 由 naked 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「赤裸；无遮盖」
由 naked 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「赤裸地；不加掩饰地」
由 naked 与 eye 复合而成，义为「肉眼观察的」

senses.title: Without any clothes on
senses.definition: not wearing any clothes, so that the whole body is open to view
senses.definitionCN: 没有穿任何衣物，整个身体都露在外面
senses.example: The child ran naked across the wet sand.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子光着身子跑过湿漉漉的沙滩。
senses.why: Old English nacod made a plain statement about the body: nothing is over the skin. That bare fact is the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nacod 只是对身体的直白陈述：皮肤上什么也没有盖。这个「什么都没有盖」的事实就是词的核心。

senses.title: Without the usual covering
senses.definition: not covered by the layer that normally protects or hides it, such as fur, leaves, paint or glass
senses.definitionCN: 缺少通常起保护或遮蔽作用的那一层，如毛、叶、漆或玻璃
senses.example: After the fire the hills stood naked in the morning light.
senses.exampleCN: 大火过后，山峦在晨光里光秃秃地立着。
senses.why: From a body without clothes the word moves to any surface missing its usual layer, because the picture is the same: a cover that ought to be there is gone.
senses.whyCN: 从没穿衣服的身体，这个词转到任何缺少惯常覆盖层的表面，画面其实一样：本该在那里的那层盖儿不见了。

senses.title: Open and undisguised
senses.definition: expressed or shown openly, with no attempt to hide it or make it softer
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达或显示出来，不做任何隐藏或软化
senses.example: He gave a naked account of how the money had disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫不掩饰地讲了那笔钱是怎么不见的。
senses.why: When nothing covers a body, nothing covers a fact either, so the word lends its image to truth, greed or aggression shown without a disguise.
senses.whyCN: 身体无物遮盖时，事实也一样无所遮盖，于是这个词把自己的画面借给了不加伪装地摆出来的真相、贪欲或侵略。

intro.en: Naked comes from a Germanic adjective for a bare body, and it has widened from clothes to any missing cover or disguise.
intro.cn: naked 源自日耳曼语中形容光裸身体的形容词，后来从衣物扩展到任何缺失的覆盖物或伪装。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning bare or unclothed is generally accepted, and it is also the distant source of Latin nudus.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「光裸、无衣」的原始印欧语词根，它也是拉丁语 nudus 的远源。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective nakwadaz meant naked or bare, without the sense of a covering that had been removed.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形容词 nakwadaz 意为光裸，并不含「被脱掉覆盖物」的意思。

items.en: Old English nacod described a body with nothing over it, and it could also describe bare ground or a bare fact.
items.cn: 古英语 nacod 描述身上无物遮盖的身体，也可以形容光秃的地面或赤裸的事实。

items.en: Middle English naked kept the same sense, and its -ed ending was already part of the word rather than a past participle.
items.cn: 中古英语的 naked 保持原义，词尾 -ed 早已是词本身的一部分，而不是过去分词标记。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for uncovered surfaces and undisguised statements, giving such phrases as naked eye, naked flame and the naked truth.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指无遮盖的表面与不加掩饰的说法，于是有 naked eye、naked flame、the naked truth 等表达。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the shape of a past participle ending in -ed but have no link in origin; the near-meaning group collects words for a body or surface with nothing on it.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带 -ed 结尾、外形相像但词源无关的词；近义组收表示身体或表面无物遮盖的词。

entries.definition: Cooked by dry heat in an oven; only the ending looks alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 在炉中用干热烤熟的；只是词尾外形相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: Made to look real when it is not; only the ending looks alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 把假的东西做得像真的；只是词尾外形相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: Morally bad, or playfully mischievous; the -ed is pronounced the same way, but the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 道德上坏的，或淘气顽皮的；其中 -ed 读音相同，但词源不同。

entries.definition: Not covered by clothes or by the usual layer.
entries.definitionCN: 没有衣物或惯常覆盖层的。

entries.definition: Not wearing clothes, especially in art or a formal description.
entries.definitionCN: 未穿衣服的，尤用于艺术或正式描述。

entries.definition: Left open to view or to harm, with no protection.
entries.definitionCN: 暴露在视线或伤害之下的，没有防护的。

entries.definition: Not wearing clothes; a formal word for the same plain fact.
entries.definitionCN: 没穿衣服的；同一个朴素事实的正式说法。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective for a bare body, and the -ed at the end is part of its history rather than a grammar ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中形容光裸身体的形容词，末尾的 -ed 属于它的历史，而不是语法词尾。

normal.en: Old English nacod is the direct ancestor, and the modern form keeps the same three consonants after the vowels shifted.
normal.cn: 古英语 nacod 是直接祖先，元音变化之后现代词形仍保留同样的三个辅音。

normal.en: The -ed is not a past tense ending: it has been inside the word since Old English, so naked does not mean having been naked.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ed 不是过去式词尾：它自古英语就在词里，所以 naked 并不表示「曾经裸过」。

normal.en: Naked eye means the eye with no lens or glass in front of it, which is the missing-cover sense at work.
normal.cn: naked eye 指前面没有镜片或玻璃的眼睛，正是「缺少覆盖层」这一义在起作用。

normal.en: Naked flame means fire with nothing around it, the same idea of a bare surface with no protection.
normal.cn: naked flame 指周围没有任何遮挡的火，同样是「裸露无防护」的意思。

normal.en: Nudus is the Latin word for bare, and it is a distant cousin of naked rather than the word that gave it birth.
normal.cn: nudus 是拉丁语中表示光裸的词，它是 naked 的远亲，而不是生出 naked 的母词。

abstract.en: Picture a body with every layer peeled away, and you have the single picture behind clothes, hills and truth.
abstract.cn: 想像一具被一层层剥去遮盖的身体，你就得到了贯穿衣物、山峦与真相的那一个画面。

abstract.en: A cover can be cloth, fur, paint or polite wording; the word treats all of them as the same thing when they are gone.
abstract.cn: 遮盖可以是布、毛、漆或客气的措辞；这个词把它们消失时的情形都看成同一件事。

abstract.en: Calling a fact naked says that no acceptable wording stands between the listener and the thing itself.
abstract.cn: 把一件事实称作 naked，等于说听者与事情本身之间没有任何可接受的措辞挡着。

examples.en: The child ran naked across the wet sand.
examples.cn: 那孩子光着身子跑过湿漉漉的沙滩。

examples.en: The planet is too faint to see with the naked eye.
examples.cn: 那颗行星太暗，用肉眼看不见。

examples.en: He gave a naked account of what had gone wrong.
examples.cn: 他毫不掩饰地讲了事情是怎么出错的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内壳的」——把外壳整个脱掉，露出里面；记住 naked 是赤裸的、无遮盖的。

root: 古英语 nacod（光裸的），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 nakwadaz，更早可追溯到原始印欧语表示「光裸」的词根，与拉丁语 nudus 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body with nothing over the skin; the senses then extend that missing cover to surfaces and to facts stated without disguise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是皮肤上无物遮盖的身体；义项再把「缺少覆盖」扩展到表面，以及不加掩饰地说出的事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: layer after layer of covering is stripped away until the body itself is all that remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层层遮盖被剥掉，最后只剩下身体本身。

branches.en: a child running into the sea with nothing on
branches.cn: 孩子身上什么也没穿，径直跑进海里

branches.en: a towel left on the sand beside a pile of clothes
branches.cn: 沙地上一条毛巾搁在一堆衣服旁

branches.en: hills stripped of grass after a fire
branches.cn: 大火之后被剥去草皮的山

branches.en: a wall with its paint gone, showing the bare brick
branches.cn: 墙面掉了漆，露出光秃秃的砖

branches.en: a sentence that hides nothing and softens nothing
branches.cn: 一句既不遮掩也不软化的话

intro.en: One Old English adjective, its English endings and compounds, and a Latin cousin that is related but not its source hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个古英语形容词、由它而来的英语词尾与复合词，以及一个相关但并非其来源的拉丁远亲，共同撑起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin nudus and its verb nudare are generally treated as distant cognates of naked, related through the same older root rather than borrowed from each other.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nudus 及其动词 nudare 一般认为与 naked 同源，通过同一个更古老的词根相关联，而不是彼此借入。

items.meaning: adjective ending, not a past tense here
items.meaningCN: 形容词词尾，此处并非过去式

definition_zh: 名字；名称；名声；命名；任命
definition_en: the word by which a person or thing is known; the reputation attached to that word; and, as a verb, to give such a word or to appoint someone
core_image: 一块木牌上刻着一个字，牌子挂上去，这件东西就有了被人呼唤的身份
scene: 村口的老槐树下，几位老人翻着泛黄的族谱，为新添的孩子挑一个合适的字。They named the baby after her grandmother, and the whole family agreed.
sceneCN: 这里是「命名、给……取名」（第 3 个义项：为某人或某物取名字）；句意是他们照着祖母的名字给宝宝取名，全家人都赞成。图中可辨识物件：族谱、老槐树、写字的木牌。

derivatives.zh: 由 name 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无名的；不知名的」
由 name 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「即；也就是」
由 name 与 plate 复合而成，义为「名牌」
由前缀 re-（重新）与 name 复合而成，义为「重新命名」

senses.title: The word by which a person or thing is known
senses.definition: the word or set of words used to identify a person, animal, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用来指认某人、某动物、某地或某物的词或词组
senses.example: She wrote her name at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她把名字写在了页面顶端。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the spoken label that calls a person over; every other sense in the word grows out of that act of naming.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是喊人时用的那个称呼；这个词的其他义项都从「叫名字」这个动作长出来。

senses.title: The reputation attached to a person or group
senses.definition: the opinion that other people have of a person, company or product, built up over time
senses.definitionCN: 他人对某人、某公司或某产品长期形成的看法
senses.example: The old bakery still has a good name in this neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老面包店在这一带仍然名声很好。
senses.why: A name stands for a person, so it can also stand for how that person is judged; the label becomes the reputation hanging on it.
senses.whyCN: 名字代表一个人，因此也能代表别人对他的评价；这个标签就变成了挂在它上面的名声。

senses.title: To give a name to someone or something
senses.definition: to give a name to a person, animal, place or thing, especially at the start of its life or use
senses.definitionCN: 给某人、某动物、某地或某物取名字，尤指在生命或使用的开端
senses.example: They named the boat after the captain's daughter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以船长的女儿为这条船命名。
senses.why: The noun supplies the label and the verb supplies the act of putting that label on a new thing, so a baby, a boat and a street can all be named.
senses.whyCN: 名词提供标签，动词提供「把标签贴到新事物上」的动作，所以婴儿、船只和街道都可以被命名。

senses.title: To appoint or specify someone
senses.definition: to officially choose someone for a position, or to state exactly which person or thing is meant
senses.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某职，或明确指出所指的是哪个人或哪件东西
senses.example: The board named her as the new director.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会任命她为新任主管。
senses.why: A name singles one person out of a crowd, so the verb can mean picking that person and putting them into a post, with the authority of the speaker behind it.
senses.whyCN: 名字把一个人从人群里单独点出来，所以这个动词可以指把那个人挑出来放到某个职位上，背后是说话者的权力在起作用。

intro.en: Name goes back to an old word for the spoken label, and its senses have spread from that label to reputation and to the act of appointing.
intro.cn: name 可追溯到表示「口头称呼」的古词，义项从这一称呼扩展到名声，再扩展到任命这一动作。

items.en: A reconstructed noun for name is widely accepted, and the same root lies behind Latin nomen and Greek onoma.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「名字」的原始印欧语名词，同一个词根也见于拉丁语 nomen 与希腊语 onoma。

items.en: The reconstructed form namô meant name, and it is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.cn: 重构形式 namô 意为名字，是英语这个词的直接祖先。

items.en: Old English nama was the everyday noun for a name, and it also supplied the verb namian, to name.
items.cn: 古英语 nama 是表示名字的日常名词，并派生出动词 namian，意为命名。

items.en: Middle English kept name as a noun and namen as a verb, and the spelling settled into its modern shape.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词 name 与动词 namen，拼写逐渐固定为现代形式。

items.en: Modern English extends the noun to reputation and the verb to official appointment, as in naming a new director.
items.cn: 现代英语把名词扩展到名声，把动词扩展到正式任命，如 naming a new director。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the word's own family and a few spellings that merely rhyme; the near-meaning group collects words for labels, titles and reputation.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的词族，以及几个只是押韵的拼写；近义组收表示标签、头衔与名声的词。

entries.definition: An adverb built from name and -ly, used to introduce an exact term.
entries.definitionCN: 由 name 加 -ly 构成的副词，用来引出确切的词语。

entries.definition: Having no name, or too ordinary or bad to be described by one.
entries.definitionCN: 没有名字的，或平凡、恶劣得无法用名字描述的。

entries.definition: Existing in name only, or relating to a name; from the Latin nomen.
entries.definitionCN: 仅名义上存在的，或与名字有关的；出自拉丁语 nomen。

entries.definition: The state of being known by many people; it rhymes with name but has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 被很多人知晓的状态；与 name 押韵，但词源不同。

entries.definition: The word attached to a book, film or person as a mark of rank.
entries.definitionCN: 附在书籍、影片或人身上、表示等级或名称的词。

entries.definition: A small piece of paper or a short word that says what something is.
entries.definitionCN: 说明某物是什么的小纸片或简短词语。

entries.definition: The general belief that people hold about someone's character or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 人们对某人品格或品质普遍持有的看法。

entries.definition: To choose someone officially for a purpose or post.
entries.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某职或用于某目的。

normalIntro.en: The word is the plain noun for a spoken label, and all its senses are different ways of using that label.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是表示「口头称呼」的朴素名词，所有义项都是使用这一称呼的不同方式。

normal.en: Old English nama is the direct ancestor, and the modern spelling keeps the same four letters at the start.
normal.cn: 古英语 nama 是直接祖先，现代拼写开头仍保留同样的四个字母。

normal.en: Namely is name plus -ly, and it introduces the exact name of the thing just mentioned.
normal.cn: namely 是 name 加 -ly，用来引出前面那件事的确切名字。

normal.en: Nameless is name plus -less, so it describes someone with no name or no distinct identity.
normal.cn: nameless 是 name 加 -less，用来形容没有名字或没有鲜明身份的人。

normal.en: Nomen is the Latin word for name, and it gives English nominal, nominate and nomination.
normal.cn: nomen 是拉丁语中的「名字」，由此有了英语的 nominal、nominate、nomination。

normal.en: In the name of is a fixed phrase in which name stands for the authority behind an act.
normal.cn: in the name of 是固定说法，这里的 name 代表一个行为背后的权力。

abstract.en: A name is a sound that makes one thing stand out from everything else, so the word is always about singling out.
abstract.cn: 名字是一种让某物从其他一切中站出来的声音，所以这个词始终关乎「单独点出」。

abstract.en: Because a name travels without the person, it can carry praise or blame long after the person is gone.
abstract.cn: 名字可以脱离本人四处流传，所以人不在场之后，它仍能承载赞誉或责备。

abstract.en: To be named to a post is to be pointed at in public, which is why the verb can mean both calling and choosing.
abstract.cn: 被任命到一个职位，就是在众人面前被点到，所以这个动词既能指称呼，也能指挑选。

examples.en: She wrote her name at the top of the page.
examples.cn: 她把名字写在了页面顶端。

examples.en: They named the boat after the captain's daughter.
examples.cn: 他们以船长的女儿为这条船命名。

examples.en: The old bakery still has a good name in this neighbourhood.
examples.cn: 那家老面包店在这一带仍然名声很好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内姆」——先记住对方的名字，才好开口叫；记住 name 是名字，也是命名。

root: 古英语 nama（名字），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 namô，更早与原始印欧语表示「名字」的词根有关；同族词有 namely、nameless、nameplate、rename 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a spoken label; the senses then divide into the label itself, the reputation it carries, the act of giving it, and the act of pointing to a chosen person.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个口头称呼；义项分出称呼本身、它承载的名声、给它命名的动作，以及把选定之人点出来的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden board is carved with one word and hung up, and from then on the thing has an identity people can call.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木牌刻上一个字、挂了起来，从此这件东西就有了可被人呼唤的身份。

branches.en: a child learning to write the letters of her own name
branches.cn: 孩子学着写下自己名字的字母

branches.en: a wooden board above a shop door with one word carved into it
branches.cn: 店门上方一块木牌上刻着一个词

branches.en: a family bakery whose sign is trusted across the district
branches.cn: 一块被整个街区信赖的老面包店招牌

branches.en: a boat taking the name of someone loved
branches.cn: 一条船得到了心爱之人的名字

branches.en: a hand raised in a meeting to point at one person
branches.cn: 会上举起手，指向某一个人

intro.en: One Old English noun, its English verb and suffixes, and a Latin family with the same older root hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个古英语名词、由它而来的英语动词与后缀，以及共享同一古老词根的拉丁词族，共同撑起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin nomen is generally treated as a cognate of name through the same older root, and it is the source of the learned words nominal and nominate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nomen 一般认为通过同一古老词根与 name 同源，并且是书面词 nominal、nominate 的来源。
