to give a name, to appoint

definition_zh: 狭窄的；狭隘的；勉强的；变窄
definition_en: measuring a small distance from side to side; limited in range or outlook; won or avoided by only a small margin; and, as a verb, to become less wide
core_image: 两堵墙向中间挤过来，人只能侧着身子从缝隙里通过
scene: 老城的巷子两边砌着高墙，一辆送货车停在巷口，司机探头量了量两侧后视镜。The lane was too narrow for the van, so the driver backed out slowly.
sceneCN: 这里是「狭窄的」（第 1 个义项：两侧之间距离小）；句意是这条巷子太窄，货车过不去，司机只好慢慢倒车出来。图中可辨识物件：高墙、后视镜、巷口的货车。

derivatives.zh: 由 narrow 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「勉强地；差一点」
由 narrow 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「狭窄；狭隘」
由 narrow 与 minded 复合而成，义为「心胸狭隘的」

senses.title: Small in width
senses.definition: measuring only a small distance from one side to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从一侧到另一侧的距离很小
senses.example: The alley is too narrow for a truck to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这条小巷太窄，卡车过不去。
senses.why: Old English nearu described a space with little room across, and that plain physical tightness is the centre of every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nearu 描述横向余量很小的空间，这种朴素的物理上的「挤」是后来所有义项的核心。

senses.title: Limited in scope or outlook
senses.definition: limited in range, sympathy or understanding, and not open to other views
senses.definitionCN: 在范围、同情心或理解力上受限，不愿接纳别的看法
senses.example: The debate was framed by a narrow set of questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论被一组狭窄的问题限制住了。
senses.why: A space with little room across becomes a mind with little room for other ideas, so the physical tightness turns into a limit on thought.
senses.whyCN: 横向余量很小的空间，会变成容不下别的想法的心胸，于是物理上的「挤」就转成了对思想的限制。

senses.title: Barely achieved or barely avoided
senses.definition: achieved by only a small margin, or avoided by only a little distance or time
senses.definitionCN: 以很小的差距取得，或只差一点就避开的
senses.example: She won the vote by a narrow margin of two votes.
senses.exampleCN: 她以两票的微弱优势赢得了表决。
senses.why: When the gap between two outcomes is narrow, the winner passes with almost no room to spare, so the word marks a close result or escape.
senses.whyCN: 当两种结果的间隙很窄时，赢的一方几乎没有余量地挤过去，所以这个词用来标记接近的结果或险境。

senses.title: To become or make less wide
senses.definition: to become less wide, or to reduce the width or range of something
senses.definitionCN: 变得不那么宽，或把某物的宽度、范围缩小
senses.example: The road narrows sharply after the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 过了桥之后，路突然变窄。
senses.why: If the adjective names a small width, the verb names the movement toward it: the two sides come closer and the space shrinks.
senses.whyCN: 如果形容词指的是小宽度，动词指的就是朝这个宽度靠拢的过程：两侧靠近，空间缩小。

intro.en: Narrow is a Germanic adjective for tight space, and the deeper root is uncertain; its senses have spread from width to scope and to a close margin.
intro.cn: narrow 是日耳曼语中形容逼仄空间的形容词，更早的词根不确定；义项从宽度扩展到范围，再扩展到微小的差距。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain, and no single reconstructed root for this Germanic adjective is agreed on.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定，学界并未就这个词的原始印欧语词根达成一致。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective narwaz meant narrow or tight, and it is the generally accepted starting point.
items.cn: 一般认为重构的形容词 narwaz 意为狭窄、逼仄，这是普遍接受的起点。

items.en: Old English nearu meant narrow and confined, and it could also name distress or oppression, the feeling of being squeezed.
items.cn: 古英语 nearu 意为狭窄、受拘束，也可指困苦或压迫，也就是被挤住的感觉。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word as narwe or narow, and its meaning settled on small width in space.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词写作 narwe 或 narow，词义固定为空间上的宽度小。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective to limited scope and close margins, and forms the verb narrow, with the phrase narrow down.
items.cn: 现代英语把形容词扩展到有限的范围与微小的差距，并造出动词 narrow，以及短语 narrow down。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that end in the same -ow sound but have no shared origin; the near-meaning group collects words for tight space and limited range.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以 -ow 音结尾、但并无共同来源的词；近义组收表示逼仄空间与有限范围的词。

entries.definition: A thin pointed stick shot from a bow; only the ending sounds alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 从弓上射出的细尖木杆，即箭；只是词尾读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The soft substance inside bones; only the ending sounds alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 骨头内部的柔软物质，即骨髓；只是词尾读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A heavy farm tool that breaks up soil; only the ending sounds alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 打碎土块的沉重农具，即耙；只是词尾读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A small brown bird common in towns; only the ending sounds alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇常见的小型褐色鸟，即麻雀；只是词尾读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Fitting closely, with little space to spare.
entries.definitionCN: 空间几乎不留余量的、紧绷的。

entries.definition: Too small and crowded for comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 狭小拥挤、让人不舒服的。

entries.definition: Kept within limits, not allowed to spread.
entries.definitionCN: 被限制在范围内、不许扩张的。

entries.definition: Small in amount or range, with a fixed boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或范围小、有固定边界的。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from tight space, and its later senses are that tightness applied to thought, to results and to movement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从逼仄的空间起步，后面的义项都是把这种「挤」用到想法、结果和动作上。

normal.en: Old English nearu meant both narrow and oppressed, which shows that tight space and tight feeling were one idea.
normal.cn: 古英语 nearu 既指狭窄也指受压迫，说明空间的挤与感受上的压抑本是同一个概念。

normal.en: Narrow-minded is narrow plus minded, so a small room in the head stands for a small range of ideas.
normal.cn: narrow-minded 是 narrow 加 minded，脑子里的小房间就成了狭窄的想法范围。

normal.en: Narrow escape keeps the picture of passing through a gap with almost no room on either side.
normal.cn: narrow escape 保留了从两侧几乎无余量的缝隙中穿过的画面。

normal.en: Narrow down adds down: the range is pushed smaller and smaller until only one thing is left.
normal.cn: narrow down 加了 down：范围被越压越小，最后只剩一样东西。

normal.en: The verb narrow is simply the adjective put into motion, so it means the sides moving closer together.
normal.cn: 动词 narrow 就是把形容词变成动作，意思是两侧互相靠近。

abstract.en: A narrow street and a narrow mind share one picture: too little room for anything else to pass.
abstract.cn: 狭窄的街道与狭隘的心胸共用一个画面：几乎没有余量让别的东西通过。

abstract.en: A narrow victory is not a small victory but one that barely fitted through the gap.
abstract.cn: 险胜并不是小胜，而是勉强从缝隙里挤过去的一次胜利。

abstract.en: Every sense measures the distance between two edges, whether those edges are walls, ideas or vote counts.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在量两条边之间的距离，无论那两条边是墙、想法还是票数。

examples.en: The lane was too narrow for the van, so the driver backed out slowly.
examples.cn: 这条巷子太窄，货车过不去，司机只好慢慢倒车出来。

examples.en: She won the vote by a narrow margin of two votes.
examples.cn: 她以两票的微弱优势赢得了表决。

examples.en: The path narrows as it climbs towards the ridge.
examples.cn: 小路向山脊爬升时越来越窄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捏肉」——两堵墙往中间捏，把肉都挤住了；记住 narrow 是狭窄的、变窄。

root: 古英语 nearu（狭窄的、受拘束的，也可指困苦），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 narwaz；更早的词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small distance between two sides; the senses then apply it to range of thought, to the margin of a result, and to the act of shrinking.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两侧之间很小的距离；义项再把它用到思想的范围、结果的差距，以及收缩这个动作上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two walls press inward until a person can only pass sideways through the gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：两堵墙向中间挤压，人只能侧着身子从缝隙里通过。

branches.en: two high walls leaving one narrow lane
branches.cn: 两堵高墙之间只留一条窄巷

branches.en: a van stopping at the mouth of an alley it cannot enter
branches.cn: 货车停在巷口，进不去

branches.en: a list of questions too short to cover the whole problem
branches.cn: 一组问题太窄，盖不住整个问题

branches.en: a vote decided by two ballots out of hundreds
branches.cn: 几百张票里靠两张定输赢

branches.en: a road pinching together as it climbs
branches.cn: 道路向上延伸时逐渐收窄

intro.en: The entry is held together by the Old English adjective, its English verb, and the endings and compounds built on the same short base.
intro.cn: 这个词条由古英语形容词、由它而来的英语动词，以及建在同一词基上的词尾与复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and its deeper root is uncertain, so no reliable Latin cognate is recorded and none is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族，更早的词根不确定，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，所以这里不列。

definition_zh: 令人厌恶的；恶劣的；下流的
definition_en: very unpleasant to the senses; severe or dangerous; and morally dirty or spiteful
core_image: 一块黏糊糊的霉斑，让人下意识缩回手
scene: 厨房角落的剩菜已经长出霉点，酸味冲得人直往后退。The milk at the back of the fridge had turned nasty.
sceneCN: 这里 nasty 是「令人厌恶的」（第 1 个义项：气味或外表使人反感）；句意为冰箱深处的牛奶已经变质发臭。图中可辨识物件：发霉的剩菜、冰箱隔层。

pos.zh: 令人厌恶的；恶劣的；下流的

derivatives.zh: 由 nasty 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「厌恶；下流」
由 nasty 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「令人厌恶地；恶意地」

senses.title: Very unpleasant to the senses
senses.titleCN: 令人厌恶的；难闻难看的
senses.definition: so unpleasant to see, smell, taste or touch that a person wants to move away from it
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉、气味、味道或触感上让人反感，使人想躲开
senses.example: A nasty smell came from the rubbish bin.
senses.exampleCN: 垃圾桶里传来一股难闻的味道。
senses.why: The earliest record of the word described something filthy, so the sense starts from physical dirt that the senses reject.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的记录指肮脏的东西，所以词义起点是感官排斥的身体污秽。

senses.title: Severe, dangerous or hard to deal with
senses.titleCN: 恶劣的；严重的；难对付的
senses.definition: used of weather, injuries, problems or events that are severe and cause real trouble
senses.definitionCN: 用于天气、伤势、问题或事件，表示严重并带来实际麻烦
senses.example: He took a nasty fall on the icy steps.
senses.exampleCN: 他在结冰的台阶上摔了很重的一跤。
senses.why: Once the word means bad to the senses, English stretches it from what smells wrong to what goes wrong, so an injury or a storm can be nasty.
senses.whyCN: 词义从「感官上不好」扩展到「事情出岔子」，受伤或风暴这类带来麻烦的事也就成了 nasty。

senses.title: Spiteful or morally dirty
senses.definition: used of words, jokes or people that are unkind, spiteful or sexually coarse
senses.definitionCN: 用于言语、玩笑或人，表示刻薄、怀有恶意或色情粗俗
senses.example: She spread nasty rumours about her rival.
senses.exampleCN: 她散布关于对手的恶意谣言。
senses.why: Filth moves easily from the body to behaviour: a dirty mouth or a dirty trick carries the same disgust that a dirty smell does.
senses.whyCN: 「脏」很容易从身体转到行为上：一张脏嘴或一个脏手段，带来的厌恶和闻到脏东西时一样。

intro.en: The word is first recorded in Middle English as nasti, and its earlier source is disputed, so the account below marks the uncertain links.
intro.cn: 这个词最早以 nasti 的形式见于中古英语，更早的来源有争议，因此下面的叙述会标明不确定的环节。

items.en: Nasti is recorded in the fourteenth century with the sense of dirty and filthy.
items.cn: 十四世纪的文献里出现 nasti，意为肮脏的、污秽的。

items.en: One common suggestion traces it to an Old French form such as nastre, meaning filthy, but the record is thin.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它追溯到意为「肮脏」的古法语形式 nastre，但证据很薄弱。

items.en: Another suggestion links it to Dutch nestig, literally nest-like, that is, dirty as a nest.
items.cn: 另一种说法把它联系到荷兰语 nestig，字面是「像鸟窝的」，即像窝一样脏。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word covers not only filth but also coarse speech and spiteful behaviour.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词不只指污秽，还指粗俗的言语和恶意的行为。

items.en: Modern English keeps the informal force of the word and uses it freely for bad weather, bad injuries and bad problems.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这个词的口语力度，广泛用于恶劣天气、严重伤势和棘手问题。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same stem; the near-meaning group collects words for disgust and unpleasantness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形式；近义组收表示厌恶与不快之感的词。

entries.definition: The noun made from nasty with -ness, meaning the quality of being nasty.
entries.definitionCN: 由 nasty 加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「厌恶；下流」。

entries.definition: The adverb made from nasty with -ly, meaning in a nasty way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 nasty 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「令人厌恶地；恶意地」。

entries.definition: A garden plant with bright flowers; its Latin name means nose-twister and only looks like nasty.
entries.definitionCN: 一种开亮色花的园艺植物；其拉丁名意为「扭鼻子」，只是拼写与 nasty 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: So unpleasant that it makes a person feel sick.
entries.definitionCN: 令人反胃的；极讨厌的。

entries.definition: Dirty, unpleasant and often smelling bad.
entries.definitionCN: 肮脏的；难闻的。

entries.definition: Not enjoyable or comfortable to experience.
entries.definitionCN: 令人不快的；不舒服的。

normalIntro.en: The word has a disputed stem and three productive English endings, which together cover the adjective, the noun and the adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词有一个来源有争议的词干和三个能产的英语词尾，分别撑起形容词、名词和副词。

normal.en: Nasti in Middle English already meant filthy, so the disgust sense is the oldest one.
normal.cn: 中古英语里的 nasti 已经表示污秽，所以「厌恶」是最老的义项。

normal.en: Nastiness and nastily are built with plain suffixes, so the family is small and easy to keep straight.
normal.cn: nastiness 与 nastily 都由普通后缀构成，词族很小，好记不乱。

normal.en: A nasty fall and nasty weather keep the same idea: something bad has happened to you.
normal.cn: nasty fall 与 nasty weather 保留同一个想法：有坏事落到你头上。

normal.en: Nasty words are called dirty words because English reuses the language of filth for meanness.
normal.cn: 恶毒的话被叫作「脏话」，因为英语把污秽的说法挪去形容刻薄。

normal.en: The comparative is nastier, not more nasty, so the ending behaves like happy and pretty.
normal.cn: 比较级是 nastier，而不是 more nasty，词尾变化和 happy、pretty 一样。

abstract.en: A word that begins with a smell and ends with a rumour shows how one kind of disgust can spread to another.
abstract.cn: 一个词从气味开始、到谣言结束，说明一种厌恶如何蔓延到另一种。

abstract.en: Nasty is English at its most physical: the nose learns the word before the mind does.
abstract.cn: nasty 是英语里最身体化的词之一：鼻子比脑子先学会它。

abstract.en: Saying that a problem is nasty quietly admits that it may beat you.
abstract.cn: 说一个问题 nasty，其实是在悄悄承认它可能把你难倒。

examples.en: The fridge had a nasty smell after the power cut.
examples.cn: 断电之后冰箱里有一股难闻的味道。

examples.en: He took a nasty fall while running down the stairs.
examples.cn: 他跑下楼梯时重重摔了一跤。

examples.en: Her nasty remarks spoiled the whole evening.
examples.cn: 她那几句恶毒的话毁了整个晚上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那个死地」——一提到那个地方就嫌恶地皱眉；记住 nasty 是令人厌恶的。

root: 中古英语 nasti（肮脏的、污秽的），来源不确定，一般认为与古法语 nastre 或荷兰语 nestig 有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is sensory disgust; from it the word reaches severe trouble and then dirty behaviour.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是感官上的厌恶；由此延伸到严重的麻烦，再伸向下流的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sticky patch of mould that makes the hand pull back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块黏糊糊的霉斑，让人下意识缩回手。

branches.en: a bin overflowing beside a warm kitchen door
branches.cn: 温热的厨房门边堆满溢出的垃圾

branches.en: a child holding its nose at a plate of spoiled food
branches.cn: 孩子闻到变质食物时捏住鼻子

branches.en: a runner flat on the ice after a bad landing
branches.cn: 跑步的人重重摔在冰面上

branches.en: a storm tearing at the roof of a coastal house
branches.cn: 风暴撕扯海边房屋的屋顶

branches.en: a whispered rumour passing from desk to desk
branches.cn: 一句悄悄话从一张桌子传到另一张桌子

intro.en: The word has a disputed stem and three productive English endings, which build the adjective, the noun and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词有一个来源有争议的词干和三个能产的英语词尾，分别构成形容词、名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate has been recorded for this word; the early source itself is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，其早期来源本身也不确定。

items.meaning: forming adjectives from nouns or stems

definition_zh: 民族；国家；全体国民；（历史用法）部落、族群
definition_en: a people who share a common origin, history or identity, especially when organized as a state
core_image: 一条手绘的边界线穿过同一片口音相同的村庄，把同一个集市分成两半
scene: 旧地图铺在桌上，一条边界线正好穿过说同一种口音的几个村庄，教书的人用手指顺着线划过。The nation was divided by a border drawn through its villages.
sceneCN: 这里 nation 指「共享同一种身份与语言的一群人」（第 2 个义项：以共同出身、语言或历史凝聚的群体，未必与国家疆界重合）；句意为这个民族被一条穿过其村庄的边界分成了两半。图中可辨识物件：旧地图、铅笔画的边界、被切开的集市、手指；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 民族；国家；全体国民（可数，复数 nations）

collocations.zh: 一个由移民构成的国家

derivatives.zh: 国家的；民族的（nation 加 -al，指属于整个民族的）
国籍；民族（national 加 -ity，指法律或族群身份）
民族主义（national 加 -ism，指以民族为中心的主张）
民族主义者；民族主义的（national 加 -ist）
收归国有；使全国化（national 加 -ize，使转为国家所有）
出生；诞生（拉丁 nasci 加 -ity，与 nation 同出「出生」词根）
本地的；本地人（拉丁 nativus，同出 nasci「出生」）

senses.title: A sovereign country
senses.definition: an independent state with its own government, territory and seat at international bodies
senses.definitionCN: 拥有自己的政府、领土与国际组织席位的独立国家
senses.example: The two nations opened embassies within a year of the ceasefire.
senses.exampleCN: 停火一年之内，这两个国家互设了大使馆。
senses.why: Because a people organized as a state is the modern default, the plain everyday sense of the word is simply 'country'.
senses.whyCN: 因为「组织成国家的一群人」是现代默认形态，所以这个词最日常的意思就是「国家」。

senses.title: A people sharing identity
senses.definition: a group held together by a common language, history or sense of belonging, whether or not it has a state
senses.definitionCN: 由共同语言、历史或归属感凝聚的群体，无论是否拥有国家
senses.example: The nation was divided by a border drawn through its villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这个民族被一条穿过其村庄的边界分成了两半。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a people born together, and that sense survives precisely where the state and the people do not match.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「同出一源的一群人」，这一意思恰恰在国家与人群不重合之处延续下来。

senses.title: The citizenry taken as one body
senses.definition: the whole body of citizens, often addressed as a single moral actor in speeches
senses.definitionCN: 全体公民的整体，常在演说中被当作单一的道义行动者来称呼
senses.example: The nation was asked to give up one holiday to fund the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 全体国民被要求放弃一个假日，为医院筹资。
senses.why: Once everyone is imagined as one body, speakers can address the whole population as a single person who decides.
senses.whyCN: 一旦所有人被想象成一个整体，演说者就能把全体人口当作一个做决定的单数人格来称呼。

senses.title: A tribe or ethnic people in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中的部落或族群
senses.definition: a people or tribe described in history and anthropology, as in the nations of the ancient Near East
senses.definitionCN: 历史学与人类学中描述的族群或部落，如古代近东诸族
senses.example: The chronicle lists the nations that sent tribute to the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这部编年史列出了向都城进贡的各族。
senses.why: Natio in Latin could mean any group of common birth, and that broad sense passed into older English historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 natio 可指任何同出一源的群体，这一宽泛含义进入了较早的英语历史写作。

senses.title: A formally recognized tribal nation
senses.titleCN: 获正式承认的原住民族
senses.definition: the official self-designation of many Native American peoples, as in the Navajo Nation
senses.definitionCN: 许多北美原住民族群的正式自称，如纳瓦霍族
senses.example: The tribal council speaks for the nation in negotiations with the federal government.
senses.exampleCN: 部落议会在与联邦政府的谈判中代表该民族发言。
senses.why: Sovereignty language was borrowed from international law, so tribes adopted 'nation' to assert a political status older than the state.
senses.whyCN: 主权话语借自国际法，因此各部落采用「nation」来主张一种比国家更古老的政治地位。

senses.title: The community of states
senses.titleCN: 国际社会中的国家共同体
senses.definition: the collectivity of states acting together, as in 'the community of nations' or 'the family of nations'
senses.definitionCN: 共同行动的各国整体，如「国际社会」「国家大家庭」
senses.example: The community of nations voted to send observers.
senses.exampleCN: 国际社会投票决定派出观察员。
senses.why: When states are treated as persons in international law, their society is naturally described as a group of nations.
senses.whyCN: 当国家在国际法中被当作人格，它们的共同体自然就被描述为一群国家。

senses.title: A student nation at older universities
senses.titleCN: 旧式大学中的学生同乡会
senses.definition: a regional association of students at historic Scandinavian and other European universities
senses.definitionCN: 北欧及欧洲其他历史悠久的大学中，按地区组成的学生团体
senses.example: He joined the northern nation and ate at its hall every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 他加入了北方学生同乡会，每晚都在其食堂吃饭。
senses.why: The word once meant simply a group of people of common origin, which is exactly what a regional student society is.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾经只表示同出一源的一群人，而按地区组成的学生团体正是如此。

senses.title: A rhetorical collective of like-minded people
senses.titleCN: 修辞上指志趣相同的一群人
senses.definition: a figurative use such as 'a nation of readers' or 'a nation of shopkeepers', naming a large group by its shared habit
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，如「阅读的民族」「店主的国家」，以共同习惯命名一大群人
senses.example: The magazine called its subscribers a nation of careful readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志把它的订户称为一个认真阅读的民族。
senses.why: The rhetorical force comes from treating a shared practice as a common birth, which is the word's original image.
senses.whyCN: 这种修辞力量来自把共同习惯当作共同出身，而这正是这个词最初的意象。

intro.en: Nation comes from a Latin noun of birth, narrowed in French toward a political people and then widened again in English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: nation 来自一个表示出生的拉丁名词，在法语中被收窄为政治意义上的国民，进入英语后又重新变宽。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nasci 'to be born' is generally thought to descend from a root meaning 'to beget', the same stock as gignere 'to produce' and genus 'race, kind'.
items.cn: nasci「出生」一般认为源自表示「生育」的词根，与 gignere「产生」、genus「种族、种类」同族。

items.en: Natio first named a birth or an origin, then a body of people of common birth; Roman writers also used it for foreigners living in one quarter of the city.
items.cn: natio 最初指出生或出身，继而指同出一源的一群人；罗马作家也用它指聚居城中一区的异邦人。

items.en: Old French nation narrowed the word to a political people or a province, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 nation 把词义收窄为政治意义上的国民或一个行省，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: English first used the word for a people of common stock, then for the whole political community of a kingdom, then for a sovereign state.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指同出一源的族群，继而指一个王国中的整体政治共同体，再指主权国家。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the word was joined to -state and -hood, and the pairing of nation and state became the normal form of political organization.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪，这个词与 state、hood 组合，民族与国家的配对成为常见的政治组织形式。

items.en: Source uncertain (dates and reconstruction): the exact point at which the word shifted from a birth-group to a sovereign state is not recorded, and the pre-Latin root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（年代与重构）：从出生群体转向主权国家的确切时点没有记载；拉丁语之前的词根形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the birth root and are constantly confused; group two holds words for the same large entity seen from different angles.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「出生」词根、极易混淆的词；第二组是从不同角度指同一大实体的词。

entries.definition: The status of belonging to a state in law, or to an ethnic group; it names a status, while nation names the group itself.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上属于某国的身份，或属于某族群的身份；它指身份，而 nation 指群体本身。

entries.definition: The adjective 'of a nation', needed before a noun; it cannot stand for the people themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「国家的、民族的」形容词，须置于名词前，不能直接代替人群本身。

entries.definition: The doctrine built on nation; it is a belief about nations, not a nation.
entries.definitionCN: 建立在 nation 之上的学说，是关于民族的信念，而非民族本身。

entries.definition: The fact of being born, or a birth scene in art; the root is literal birth rather than a political people.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生这一事实，或艺术中的诞生场景；词根取「出生」字面义，而非政治人群。

entries.definition: The political and legal apparatus with borders and sovereignty; a nation may exist without one, a state may hold several.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有边界与主权的政治法律机构；民族可以没有国家，国家也可以包含多个民族。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a land and its people; it stresses territory rather than shared identity.
entries.definitionCN: 指一片土地及其人民的日常用词，侧重领土而非共同身份。

entries.definition: A body of persons considered together; it can mean the same as nation but carries no claim to a state.
entries.definitionCN: 被整体看待的一群人；可与民族同义，但不含建国主张。

entries.definition: A group defined by ancestry, language and culture; it is the social-science term where nation carries political weight.
entries.definitionCN: 以祖先、语言与文化界定的群体；这是社会科学术语，而 nation 带有政治分量。

root: 拉丁 natio「出生、出身、族群」，出自 nasci「出生」；与 gignere「产生」、genus「种族」一般认为是同一词族。英语 nation 兼指民族与国家，因为二者常被视为一体。

branches.en: ONE BODY: the citizenry is addressed as a single moral person.

definition_en: born in or belonging naturally to a particular place, and hence original or inborn
core_image: 一株只长在这面山坡的野花，根须抓住本地的碎石，移栽到别处便枯死
scene: 这面山坡上只长这一种野花，移栽到别处总活不成。The plant is native to this slope and nowhere else.
sceneCN: 这里 native 指原产于某地的（第 2 个义项：天然属于某地）；句意为这种植物原产于这面山坡，别处没有。

天生的；固有的（指与生俱来的性质）
（计算机）原生的（为某平台原生开发）

senses.title: Born in a place
senses.definition: having been born in a particular place or country
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地方或国家出生的
senses.example: She is a native of the coastal town and knows every lane.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这座海滨小镇本地出生的人，认得每一条小巷。
senses.why: The Latin root is birth itself; the adjective begins as a plain statement about where someone was born.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本身就是「出生」；这个形容词起初只是关于出生地的平实陈述。

senses.title: Belonging to a place naturally
senses.definition: growing or living naturally in a region and not introduced from elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 在某地区自然生长或生活，而非从别处引入的
senses.example: The plant is native to this slope and nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物原产于这面山坡，别处没有。
senses.why: The same birth relation applies to species: a plant is 'born' in its range and does not need a person to place it there.
senses.whyCN: 同样的出生关系也适用于物种：植物在其分布区内「出生」，不需要人把它放到那里。

senses.title: Indigenous person
senses.definition: a member of the peoples who lived in a territory before later settlers
senses.definitionCN: 在后来定居者之前就生活于某片土地的民族的成员
senses.example: The treaty was signed with the native inhabitants, not with the settlers.
senses.exampleCN: 条约是与原住居民签订的，而不是与定居者。
senses.why: The noun turns the birth relation into a political identity, and modern usage often prefers indigenous for this sense.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式把出生关系变成政治身份；现代用法在这一义项上更常用「原住民族」这一说法。

senses.title: Inborn quality
senses.definition: present from birth rather than learned or acquired
senses.definitionCN: 出生时就有、而非习得或获得的
senses.example: He has a native talent for hearing pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 他有分辨音高的天赋。
senses.why: If native means born with a place, it can also mean born with a quality; the metaphor moves from location to nature.
senses.whyCN: 如果这个词指「生在某地」，它也能指「生来带有某种性质」；这个比喻从地点移到了天性。

senses.title: Unmixed material
senses.definition: found in a pure form in nature, as of metals
senses.definitionCN: 在自然界以纯净形态存在，如某些金属
senses.example: The riverbed holds native copper, not ore.
senses.exampleCN: 河床里有天然铜，而不是矿石。
senses.why: A metal 'native to the earth' is one that nature left uncombined; the sense narrows to chemical purity.
senses.whyCN: 「生在大地之中」的金属，就是自然留下、未经化合的那种；词义收窄到化学纯度。

senses.title: Built for a platform
senses.definition: designed to run directly on a particular operating system or device
senses.definitionCN: 为某一操作系统或设备直接运行而设计的
senses.example: The native app opens faster than the web version.
senses.exampleCN: 原生应用比网页版打开得更快。
senses.why: Computing borrows the word for belonging: software native to a system needs no translator layer.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了「属于」这一含义：属于某系统的软件不需要转译层。

senses.title: First-learned language
senses.definition: the language a person acquired in childhood, often called the mother tongue
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在童年习得的语言，常称为母语
senses.example: Her native language is not the one she writes in now.
senses.exampleCN: 她的母语并不是她现在写作所用的语言。
senses.why: Language is acquired at birth-time, so the adjective marks the earliest layer of speech rather than national origin.
senses.whyCN: 语言在出生时期被习得，因此这个形容词标记言语的最早层次，而非国籍。

senses.title: A local resident
senses.definition: a person who lives in a place by birth rather than by recent arrival
senses.definitionCN: 因出生而居住在某地、而非近期到来的人
senses.example: The shopkeeper is a native but the cook arrived last year.
senses.exampleCN: 店主是本地人，厨师则是去年才来的。
senses.why: In everyday use the noun simply contrasts old residents with newcomers, with no legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 在日常用法中，这个名词只是把老居民与新来者对照，没有法律分量。

senses.title: The colonial label
senses.definition: the dated and often demeaning use of the noun for colonised peoples
senses.definitionCN: 殖民时代用来指被殖民人群的过时且常含贬抑的名词用法
senses.example: Colonial reports used the noun in a way that modern editors avoid.
senses.exampleCN: 殖民报告使用这个名词的方式，现代编辑会回避。
senses.why: A neutral birth word can be turned into a category of rule; this sense names that history rather than endorsing it.
senses.whyCN: 一个中性的出生词可以被变成统治的类别；这个义项命名那段历史，而非认可它。

intro.en: Native comes from Latin nativus 'innate, born', from nasci 'to be born', whose older form gnasci belongs to the gen- root seen in genus and generate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: native 来自拉丁 nativus「天生的、出生的」，源自动词 nasci「出生」，其更早形式 gnasci 属于 gen- 词根，该词根也见于 genus 与 generate。年代均为约数。

items.en: Nasci 'to be born, to arise' is a deponent verb; its older form gnasci shows the initial g that survives in cognate words.
items.cn: nasci「出生、产生」是异态动词；其更早形式 gnasci 显示出词首的 g，这个 g 在同族词中保留下来。

items.en: Nativus meant 'innate, natural, born with one', and also 'of birth'. It could describe a person born in a place and a quality present from birth.
items.cn: nativus 意为「天生的、自然的、生来带有的」，也指「出生的」。它既能描述生于某地的人，也能描述与生俱来的性质。

items.en: The gen- root 'to be born, beget' is reconstructed; it also underlies genus, genius, generate and nation. The reconstruction is standard but the exact ablaut grades are reconstructed forms.
items.cn: 表示「出生、生育」的 gen- 词根属重构；它也是 genus、genius、generate 与 nation 的基础。这一重构是通行的，但具体的元音交替形式均属重构。

items.en: Old French natif carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of inborn and later of local birth.
items.cn: 古法语 natif 在十四世纪把该词带入英语，先表示「天生的」，后表示「本地出生的」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the noun was used by settlers for the peoples they colonised, a usage now recognised as demeaning and largely replaced.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个名词被定居者用来指他们所殖民的人群；这一用法如今被认定为贬抑性的，且多被取代。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact pre-Latin shape of the birth root is a reconstruction, and the date at which the computing sense appeared is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个「出生」词根在拉丁语之前的确切形状属重构形式；计算机义项出现的年代也没有精确固定。

note.en: Group one separates near neighbours from the same birth root; group two holds words for original belonging.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一「出生」词根的近邻词；第二组表示原初归属。

entries.definition: A people or state, from the same birth root; it names a collectivity, while native names a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 民族或国家，同出「出生」词根；它命名一个集合，而 native 命名一种关系。

entries.definition: Relating to birth, as in natal care; it is medical and temporal, with no sense of belonging to a place.
entries.definitionCN: 与出生有关的，如产后护理；它属医学与时间用法，不含「属于某地」之意。

entries.definition: A birth, especially the Nativity; it names the event rather than a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 出生，尤指耶稣诞生；它命名事件，而非性质。

entries.definition: Lacking experience; it comes from French naive, from Latin nativus 'natural', but developed the sense of unworldly.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏经验的；来自法语 naive，再上溯拉丁 nativus「自然的」，但发展出「不通世故」之义。

entries.definition: Native to a territory before settlers; it is the preferred term in law and advocacy.
entries.definitionCN: 先于定居者而原产于某地；它是法律与倡议中更受青睐的说法。

entries.definition: Of a nearby place; it says nothing about birth or priority.
entries.definitionCN: 属于附近地方的；不涉及出生或时间在先。

entries.definition: Present from birth as a quality; it covers only the innate sense of native.
entries.definitionCN: 作为性质与生俱来的；只覆盖 native 的天生义。

entries.definition: Found only in one region, often of species or disease; it stresses restriction rather than birth.
entries.definitionCN: 仅见于某一地区，常用于物种或疾病；强调局限，而非出生。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real birth root, its real relatives and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「出生」词根、其真实同族词与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Native means born: the same root gives nation, natal and nativity.
normal.cn: native 意为「出生的」：同一词根给出 nation、natal、nativity。

normal.en: A plant native to a slope is 'born' there; a native speaker was 'born into' the language.
normal.cn: 原产山坡的植物是在那里「出生」的；母语者是被「生进」那门语言的。

normal.en: Native copper is metal nature left unmixed, the chemical version of 'belonging to the earth'.
normal.cn: 天然铜是自然留下、未经混合的金属，即「属于大地」的化学版本。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: native speaker, native species, native to, a native of.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出范围：母语者、本地物种、原产于、本地出生的人。

normal.en: The plural natives is neutral only for local residents; for peoples, indigenous is safer.
normal.cn: 复数 natives 只在指本地居民时中性；指民族时，用 indigenous 更稳妥。

abstract.en: Picture a root system that refuses to hold in foreign gravel.
abstract.cn: 想象一套根须，在陌生的碎石里怎么也抓不住。

abstract.en: Picture a word learned at a kitchen table before any classroom.
abstract.cn: 想象一个在饭桌旁、任何教室之前就学会的词。

abstract.en: Picture software that speaks the machine's own language without an interpreter.
abstract.cn: 想象一种软件，不用翻译就说着机器自己的语言。

examples.en: The eucalyptus is native to Australia but grows all over the world now.
examples.cn: 桉树原产于澳大利亚，如今却长遍世界。

examples.en: A native speaker may still not know why a sentence is grammatical.
examples.cn: 母语者仍可能不知道一个句子为何合乎语法。

examples.en: The app was rebuilt as a native version for each platform.
examples.cn: 这个应用被重做成各平台的原生版本。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow birth from a place to species, peoples, innate qualities, pure metals, software platforms, first languages, local residency and the colonial label.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着「出生」展开：从出生地，到物种、民族、天生性质、纯净金属、软件平台、母语、本地居民，以及殖民时代的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a root that holds only in its own gravel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一套只在本乡碎石里才抓得住的根。

branches.en: BIRTH AT TWO SCALES: born in a place, and born into a language.
branches.cn: 两种尺度的出生：生于某地，以及生入一门语言。

branches.en: NATURE AND HISTORY: a species belongs to its range, and a people belongs before settlers.
branches.cn: 自然与历史：物种属于其分布区，民族则先于定居者而属于那里。

branches.en: INWARD AND PURE: a quality present at birth, and a metal left unmixed.
branches.cn: 向内与纯净：出生时就在的性质，以及未经混合的金属。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: software native to a system needs no translator.
branches.cn: 机器：属于某系统的软件不需要转译。

branches.en: RESIDENT AND LABEL: the neutral local, and the colonial noun that modern usage rejects.
branches.cn: 居民与标签：中性的本地人，以及现代用法拒斥的殖民名词。

intro.en: Native is a Latin adjective of birth; its stem also builds a family of English words about origins.
intro.cn: native 是表示「出生」的拉丁形容词；其词干还构成一批关于来源的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nasci and nativus supply the base; the same gen- root reaches English in genus, generate, nation and natal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nasci 与 nativus 提供基础；同一 gen- 词根经 genus、generate、nation 与 natal 进入英语。

definition_zh: 自然的；天然的；天生的；正常的
definition_en: existing in nature rather than made by people; also inborn, and normal or expected
core_image: 一株野草从石缝里自己钻出来，没有人去栽种
scene: 山脚下有一片从未开垦的林地，藤蔓顺着倒下的树干自己爬上去。The reserve protects the natural habitat of the local birds.
sceneCN: 这里 natural 是「自然的、天然的」（第 1 个义项：非人造）；句意为保护区守护当地鸟类的天然栖息地。图中可辨识物件：倒木、藤蔓、林地。

senses.title: Existing in nature, not made by people
senses.definition: found in nature and produced without human making or control
senses.definitionCN: 存在于自然界、并非由人制造或控制而产生的
senses.example: The park protects the natural habitat of the birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园保护着鸟类的天然栖息地。
senses.why: The Latin noun natura names the way things are born and grow, so natural starts from what comes into being without human hands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 natura 指事物出生、生长的样子，所以 natural 的起点是未经人手而生成的东西。

senses.title: Inborn rather than learned
senses.definition: present in a person or animal from birth and not learned
senses.definitionCN: 人与生俱来、并非后天学到的
senses.example: She has a natural gift for languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生就有语言天赋。
senses.why: If natura is the way something is born, a quality that arrives at birth is literally natural, which is why talent can be natural.
senses.whyCN: 既然 natura 指事物出生时的样子，出生就带来的特质自然就是「天生的」，天赋也就能说成 natural。

senses.title: Normal and to be expected
senses.definition: what normally happens and therefore does not surprise anyone
senses.definitionCN: 按常理会发生，因此不令人意外
senses.example: It is natural to feel nervous before a test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前感到紧张是正常的。
senses.why: What follows nature follows a regular course, so natural extends from how things grow to how things usually happen.
senses.whyCN: 顺着本性发展的东西有其常规，于是 natural 从「事物如何生长」扩展到「事情通常如何发生」。

senses.title: Relaxed and not put on
senses.definition: used of behaviour or manner that is easy and sincere, with no pretending
senses.definitionCN: 形容举止轻松真诚，不装样子
senses.example: His smile was warm and natural.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑容温暖而自然。
senses.why: A person who behaves as nature made them, without forcing a pose, looks natural, which gives the word its social sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个人按本性行事、不硬摆姿势，看上去就是 natural，这就是这个词的社交义。

intro.en: Natural comes from the Latin noun natura, which itself grows out of nasci, to be born.
intro.cn: natural 来自拉丁名词 natura，而 natura 又由 nasci（出生）生长出来。

items.en: Nasci meant to be born, the root behind nature, native and innate.
items.cn: nasci 意为出生，是 nature、native、innate 共同的根。

items.en: Natura named the character or course of things, what a thing is born to be.
items.cn: natura 指事物的本性或进程，即事物生来就该有的样子。

items.en: Naturalis meant belonging to nature or coming from birth.
items.cn: naturalis 意为属于自然的，或与生俱来的。

items.en: Old French naturel passed into Middle English natural, keeping both the world sense and the inborn sense.
items.cn: 古法语 naturel 进入中古英语作 natural，同时保留「自然界」和「天生」两义。

items.en: Modern English adds the meanings normal and unaffected, which grow from the idea of following nature.
items.cn: 现代英语又添「正常」与「不做作」两义，都由「顺其自然」的想法长出。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same birth stem; the near-meaning group collects words for what is normal and inborn.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「出生」词干上的词；近义组收表示正常与天生的词。

entries.definition: The physical world and the character built into a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 物质世界，以及事物内在的本性。

entries.definition: Born in a particular place, or belonging there by birth.
entries.definitionCN: 在某个地方出生的；原产的。

entries.definition: Present in a person from birth, not learned.
entries.definitionCN: 人与生俱来的，并非学来的。

entries.definition: What is usual and expected, with nothing odd about it.
entries.definitionCN: 通常而合乎预期的，没有异常之处。

entries.definition: Grown or produced without artificial chemicals or processes.
entries.definitionCN: 不使用人工化学物或工艺而生长、生产的。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by a Latin noun of birth and three English endings that build an adverb, a noun and a verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由一个表示「出生」的拉丁名词和三个英语词尾支撑，分别构成副词、名词和动词。

normal.en: Natura is Latin for the way things are born and grow, so natural is first about the world, not about people.
normal.cn: natura 是拉丁语中事物出生、生长的样子，所以 natural 首先说的是世界，而不是人。

normal.en: Naturally adds -ly, and it doubles as an answer word meaning of course.
normal.cn: naturally 加 -ly 构成，它还有一个「当然」的用法。

normal.en: Native and innate share the same birth root, one meaning born in a place, the other born in a person.
normal.cn: native 与 innate 共用同一个「出生」的词根，一个指在某地出生，一个指天生。

normal.en: Natural gas and natural resources are fixed phrases, so natural here means unprocessed, not easy.
normal.cn: natural gas 与 natural resources 是固定搭配，这里的 natural 指未经加工，而不是轻松。

normal.en: A natural death means death by age or illness, not by accident or violence.
normal.cn: natural death 指因年老或疾病死亡，而不是意外或暴力致死。

abstract.en: A word that begins with the world and ends with good manners shows how deeply English ties sincerity to nature.
abstract.cn: 一个词从自然界开始、到得体举止结束，说明英语把「真诚」紧紧系在「自然」上。

abstract.en: Calling something natural is often a quiet claim that nothing has been added to it.
abstract.cn: 说某物是 natural，常常是在悄悄声明没有往里面添加别的东西。

abstract.en: When a gift is called natural, praise and modesty arrive in the same word.
abstract.cn: 当一份天赋被叫作 natural，赞美与谦逊同时落在同一个词里。

examples.en: This valley is one of the few natural habitats left for the species.
examples.cn: 这条山谷是该物种仅存的几处天然栖息地之一。

examples.en: He has a natural ability to make strangers feel at ease.
examples.cn: 他天生就有让陌生人放松的本事。

examples.en: It is natural to miss home during the first month abroad.
examples.cn: 出国头一个月想家是正常的。

senses.title: In nature's own way
senses.titleCN: 以自然的方式：不按人为规矩来
senses.definition: in a way that follows nature rather than human design or convention
senses.definitionCN: 依照自然而非人为设计或惯例的方式进行
senses.example: The river runs naturally through the valley, without any concrete banks.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河自然地流过山谷，两岸没有水泥护岸。
senses.why: The adverb describes the manner of an action: it happens as nature would have it, so the absence of human arrangement is the point.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词描述动作的方式：事情按自然本来的样子发生，所以“没有人为安排”正是重点。

senses.title: From birth, by temperament
senses.titleCN: 天生地：生来就带着的本事或性情
senses.definition: as a result of inborn ability or character rather than training
senses.definitionCN: 出于与生俱来的能力或性格，而非后天训练
senses.example: She naturally remembers faces, even ones she has seen only once.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生记得住面孔，哪怕只见过一次。
senses.why: Here the adverb points to the origin of an ability: the talent is treated as part of the person's constitution, not as an acquired skill.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词指向能力的来源：这份才能被视为个人禀赋的一部分，而不是后天习得的技能。

senses.title: As you would expect
senses.titleCN: 理所当然：事情本就该这样
senses.definition: as is reasonable or unsurprising, given the circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 在那种情形下合乎情理、并不令人意外
senses.example: Naturally, the children were excited the night before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前一晚孩子们很兴奋，这是理所当然的。
senses.why: This sense is about inference, not nature: the speaker says the outcome follows so obviously that no explanation is needed.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项关乎推理而非自然：说话者表示结果显然如此，根本无须解释。

senses.title: Without human help
senses.titleCN: 未经人工干预：自己长出来的
senses.definition: happening or existing without cultivation, manufacture, or intervention
senses.definitionCN: 在没有栽培、制造或人为干预的情况下发生或存在
senses.example: The valley is naturally protected from strong winds by its surrounding hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷因四周的丘陵而天然不受强风侵袭。
senses.why: The word marks a cause that is not human: whatever produced the result was already there, so no one deserves credit or blame for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出非人为的原因：产生结果的东西本来就存在，因此无人该为此受功或受责。

senses.title: Without pretending
senses.titleCN: 不做作：不摆姿态、不加表演
senses.definition: in a relaxed and sincere manner that shows no affectation
senses.definitionCN: 以放松而真诚的方式，不显出做作
senses.example: On camera she laughed naturally, not the way she laughed in advertisements.
senses.exampleCN: 镜头前她笑得很自然，不是广告里那种笑法。
senses.why: Praise of natural behaviour measures the distance between a person and a performance; the smaller the distance, the more naturally it is done.
senses.whyCN: 称赞举止自然，衡量的是“人”与“表演”之间的距离；距离越小，就做得越自然。

senses.title: By logical consequence
senses.titleCN: 顺理成章：顺着前提必然走到这里
senses.definition: as a necessary or logical consequence of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 作为先前事情必然或合乎逻辑的结果
senses.example: Naturally, a longer delay meant a higher final cost.
senses.exampleCN: 工期拖得更久，最终成本自然更高。
senses.why: The sense borrows the idea of nature as an inevitable order and applies it to reasoning: given the premise, the conclusion could hardly be otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项借用了“自然是一种必然秩序”的观念，并把它用于推理：前提既定，结论几乎不可能不是这样。

senses.title: Found in the wild
senses.titleCN: 天然存在：自然界里本来就有
senses.definition: occurring in nature rather than being made or introduced by people
senses.definitionCN: 存在于自然界，而非由人制造或引入
senses.example: The element is naturally present in seawater at a very low concentration.
senses.exampleCN: 这种元素天然存在于海水中，浓度极低。
senses.why: In science the word distinguishes a substance that was already in the environment from one released or synthesised by humans.

senses.title: Easily and smoothly
senses.titleCN: 从容自如：做起来不费劲
senses.definition: with ease and fluency, as if no effort were required
senses.definitionCN: 轻松流畅地，仿佛不需要用力
senses.example: After a month of practice, the steps came naturally to him.
senses.exampleCN: 练了一个月后，这些步骤他做起来已从容自如。
senses.why: Skill that has become second nature no longer shows the seams of conscious control; the adverb reports that ease rather than describing the world.
senses.whyCN: 熟练到成为第二天性时，动作不再露出刻意控制的痕迹；这个副词报告的是这种轻松，而不是在描述世界。

intro.en: Naturally is natural plus the adverb suffix -ly. Natural goes back through French to Latin natura and the verb nasci, to be born.
intro.cn: naturally 是 natural 加副词后缀 -ly。natural 经法语上溯至拉丁语 natura 与动词 nasci“出生”。

items.en: Nasci meant to be born or to arise. From it came natura, the condition and character one has at birth.
items.cn: nasci 意为“出生、产生”。由它派生出 natura，指出生时的状况与禀性。

items.en: Naturalis described what belongs to nature or comes from it, as opposed to what art or human skill produces.
items.cn: naturalis 描述属于自然或来自自然的东西，与技艺或人力所产相对。

items.en: Old French naturel kept both senses: the physical world and a person's inborn disposition.
items.cn: 古法语 naturel 保留两层含义：物质世界，以及人的固有性情。

items.en: English formed adverbs with -ly from Old English -lice. Naturally therefore means 'in a natural manner' before it means 'of course'.
items.cn: 英语用 -ly（古英语 -lice）构成副词。因此 naturally 先表示“以自然的方式”，之后才引申出“当然”。

items.en: The 'as expected' sense grew out of the idea that nature follows a fixed order: what is natural is also what regularly happens.
items.cn: “如所预料”义由“自然遵循固定秩序”的观念生长出来：合乎自然的，也就是经常发生的。

items.en: Science writing added naturally occurring; speech and performance writing added the sense of ease without affectation.
items.cn: 科学写作发展出 naturally occurring（天然存在）；言语与表演领域则发展出“从容不做作”的义项。

note.en: The first group shares the nature root; the second compares adverbs that describe how an action comes about.
note.cn: 第一组共享 nature 词根；第二组比较几个描述“动作如何发生”的副词。

entries.definition: existing in nature, inborn, or normal. It modifies a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 自然界存在的、天生的或正常的；修饰名词。

entries.definition: the physical world, or the essential character of something.
entries.definitionCN: 物质世界，或某物的本质特性。

entries.definition: the quality of being natural or free from affectation.
entries.definitionCN: 自然、不做作的性质。

entries.definition: as everyone knows or expects. It marks the obviousness of a fact, not its origin.
entries.definitionCN: 众所周知或如人所料；标出事实的显然，而不涉其来源。

entries.definition: in a way that cannot be avoided. It is stronger than naturally and implies necessity.
entries.definitionCN: 以无法避免的方式；比 naturally 更强，含必然性。

entries.definition: by automatic animal impulse rather than thought. It applies to living creatures.
entries.definitionCN: 凭本能的自动冲动而非思考；适用于生物。

entries.definition: from one's own impulse, without planning; also happening without external cause.
entries.definitionCN: 出于自身冲动、未经计划；也指无外在原因地发生。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: natural + -ly. The suffix simply turns the adjective into an adverb, so the meaning tracks natural.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：natural 加 -ly。后缀只是把形容词变成副词，词义随 natural 走。

normal.en: Natural + -ly: do it the way nature would, with no scaffolding.
normal.cn: natural 加 -ly：照自然的方式做，不加支架。

normal.en: A talent you never trained comes naturally; a habit you drilled also comes naturally after enough practice.
normal.cn: 没练过的才能，说起来就是“生来就会”；练够了的习惯，用起来也同样轻松自如。

normal.en: In a chemistry paper, naturally means it was already in the water.
normal.cn: 在化学论文里，naturally 表示它本来就在水里。

normal.en: Naturally at the start of a sentence usually means 'as you can guess'.
normal.cn: naturally 放在句首，通常就是“你猜也猜得到”。

normal.en: A good actor makes a rehearsed line sound naturally spoken.
normal.cn: 好演员能把排练过的台词说得像自然说出的一样。

abstract.en: Nature and reason share one adverb: what always happens and what must follow are felt to be the same order.
abstract.cn: 自然与理性共用一个副词：总会发生的事与必然推出的事，被感受为同一种秩序。

abstract.en: Saying 'naturally' hides who arranged the conditions; it presents a result as if no one had chosen it.
abstract.cn: 说 naturally 会隐藏是谁安排了条件：它把结果呈现得好像无人选择过。

abstract.en: Effortless skill is nature edited by years of practice, and the adverb keeps the editing out of sight.
abstract.cn: 举重若轻的技艺，是被多年练习剪辑过的自然；而这个副词把剪辑痕迹藏在镜头外。

examples.en: The lake is naturally too cold for swimming until late June.
examples.cn: 这个湖天然太冷，要到六月下旬才适合游泳。

examples.en: Naturally, the students who read the whole book did better on the essay question.
examples.cn: 读过整本书的学生在论述题上表现更好，这是理所当然的。

examples.en: She stepped onto the stage and began to speak naturally, as if the audience were old friends.
examples.cn: 她走上台，自然地开口，仿佛观众都是老朋友。

dict_mnemonic.text: natural（自然的）+ ly（地）——自然地；事情按常理发展，也就成了“当然”。

root: 由 natural（自然的，源自拉丁语 natura“出生、本性”，出自 nasci“出生”）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，本义为“以自然的方式”，后引申为“天生地、理所当然地”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of naturally. One thread runs through them: something happens without visible human arrangement. That can mean without cultivation, without training, without affectation, or simply without any need to explain.
sensesIntro.cn: naturally 的八个义项由一条线串起：事情发生，却看不出人为安排。这可以指未经栽培、未经训练、不加做作，或干脆无须解释。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed in bare soil, growing toward the light with no stake and no instruction.
core.cn: 核心意象：裸土里的一粒种子，没有支架也没有指令，自己朝光生长。

branches.en: WITHOUT HUMAN DESIGN: a free river and an element already in seawater both exist before anyone acts.
branches.cn: 无人为设计：自由流淌的河与海水中本就存在的元素，都在人行动之前就已存在。

branches.en: WITHOUT TRAINING: inborn memory and practised ease both look as if no learning took place.
branches.cn: 未经训练：天生的记忆力与练成的从容，看起来都像没有学习过。

branches.en: WITHOUT EXPLANATION: 'as you would expect' and 'by consequence' both present the result as obvious.
branches.cn: 无须解释：“如你所料”与“顺理成章”都把结果呈现为显然。

branches.en: WITHOUT CULTIVATION: shelter and protection supplied by terrain rather than by builders.
branches.cn: 未经栽培：由地形而非建造者提供的遮蔽与保护。

branches.en: WITHOUT PERFORMANCE: behaviour that does not advertise itself as behaviour.
branches.cn: 不加表演：举止不把自己标榜为“举止”。

intro.en: Naturally is natural plus -ly, the standard English adverb suffix. The family spreads through -ness, -ism, -ist, -ize, and the prefix un-.
intro.cn: naturally 是 natural 加 -ly，即英语标准副词后缀。词族再通过 -ness、-ism、-ist、-ize 与否定前缀 un- 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is nasci, to be born, giving natura and naturalis. English -ly descends from Old English -lice, not from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 nasci“出生”，由此得到 natura 与 naturalis。英语 -ly 则源自古英语 -lice，并非来自拉丁语。

items.meaning: in a natural manner; as expected

items.exampleCN: 这条小径顺着山脊自然向上延伸。

items.meaning: the quality of being natural or unaffected

items.exampleCN: 她声音里的自然感让这段录音容易让人信服。

items.meaning: the view that nature is all of reality
items.meaningCN: 自然即全部现实的学说
items.example: Naturalism rejects explanations that step outside nature.
items.exampleCN: 自然主义拒绝越出自然之外的解释。

items.meaning: a field researcher of living things
items.meaningCN: 野外研究生物的人；博物学家
items.example: The naturalist noted the first migrants of spring.
items.exampleCN: 这位博物学家记下了春天第一批迁徙的鸟。

items.meaning: to make natural, or to establish a species or word as native
items.meaningCN: 使自然化；使物种或词语归化
items.example: The plant naturalized quickly in the wet soil.
items.exampleCN: 这种植物在湿土中很快归化了。

items.meaning: contrary to nature or to normal feeling

items.exampleCN: 午夜天空的亮度显得反常。

items.meaningCN: 存在于自然秩序之外的；超自然的

senses.title: Badly behaved, especially of a child
senses.definition: used of a child or pet that does not do what it is told and breaks rules in a mild way
senses.definitionCN: 用于孩子或宠物，指不听大人的话、轻微违反规矩
senses.example: The naughty puppy hid my slippers under the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 这只调皮的小狗把我的拖鞋藏到了床底下。
senses.why: The word grew out of naught, meaning nothing or no good, so a naughty child is one whose behaviour falls short of what is good.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 naught（无、没什么好）长出来，所以 naughty 的孩子就是行为「不及于善」、不够听话的孩子。

senses.title: Mildly disobedient in a playful way
senses.titleCN: 顽皮的；带点恶作剧意味的
senses.definition: used of playful rule-breaking that is charming rather than truly bad, as in an extra dessert or a skipped chore
senses.definitionCN: 用于带乐趣的小小违规，比如多吃一份甜品或偷懒不做家务，并非真正恶劣
senses.example: She had a second slice of cake and said it was very naughty of her.
senses.exampleCN: 她多吃了第二块蛋糕，说自己真是太不乖了。
senses.why: Because the blame in naughty is mild and affectionate, adults borrow it for small guilty pleasures that break no real rules.
senses.whyCN: naughty 带的责备很轻、还带疼爱，于是大人也借它来形容无伤大雅的小小放纵。

senses.title: Rude or sexual in language or humour
senses.definition: used of jokes, words or pictures that deal with sex in a way polite talk avoids
senses.definitionCN: 用于笑话、词语或图片，指以礼貌言语避谈的方式涉及性
senses.example: The comedian told a few naughty jokes at the end of the show.
senses.exampleCN: 喜剧演员在演出快结束时讲了几个下流的笑话。
senses.why: Adult speech stretches the child's small sin into the grown-up one: what is not said in public is naughty, so the word slides to rude humour.
senses.whyCN: 小孩的小小出格被放大为成年人的出格：不宜公开说出口的话就是 naughty，词义于是滑向下流幽默。

intro.en: The word is built on the old English noun naught, meaning nothing or evil, with the adjective ending -y, so its history is plain and well recorded.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在古英语名词 naught（意为「无、恶」）之上，加形容词词尾 -y 构成，源流清楚、记录完整。

items.en: The root behind naught is a reconstructed Germanic compound of not and aught, giving the sense of no thing at all.
items.cn: naught 的词根一般重构为日耳曼语的复合形式，由 not 与 aught 合成，意为「什么都没有」。

items.en: Forms such as nawt and nawiht meant nothing, and by extension also evil or wickedness.
items.cn: 古英语里 nawt、nawiht 等形式意为「无」，引申也指「恶、坏事」。

items.en: Naught keeps both senses: nothing, and moral badness, which prepares the ground for the adjective.
items.cn: 中古英语里 naught 同时保有「无」与「恶」两义，为形容词的诞生做好了铺垫。

items.en: Naughty is first recorded in the fourteenth century, meaning having naught, that is, good for nothing or wicked.
items.cn: 十四世纪首次记录 naughty，意为「一无所有」，即毫无价值、品行恶劣。

items.en: The severe sense of morally bad softens, and the word settles on children and pets that disobey.
items.cn: 「品行恶劣」的严厉义逐渐软化，这个词固定下来专指不听话的孩子和宠物。

items.en: Modern English keeps the mild sense for children and adds the adult sense of rude or sexual humour.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了针对孩子的轻微义，又添了指粗俗、涉性幽默的成人用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the word family built on naught; the near-meaning group collects words for misbehaviour and rude humour.
note.cn: 形近组收以 naught 为核心的词族；近义组收表示不听话与粗俗幽默的词。

entries.definition: An old word for nothing or zero, the noun that naughty is built on.
entries.definitionCN: naughty 所从出的名词，古旧用法，意为「无；零」。

entries.definition: The adverb made from naughty with -ly, meaning in a naughty way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 naughty 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「调皮地；不听话地」。

entries.definition: The noun made from naughty with -ness, meaning the quality of being naughty.
entries.definitionCN: 由 naughty 加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「淘气；顽皮」。

entries.definition: Playfully causing trouble, especially of children who enjoy small pranks.
entries.definitionCN: 顽皮的；爱恶作剧的，尤指以小捣蛋为乐的孩子。

entries.definition: Refusing to obey rules or the people in charge, a more formal word than naughty.
entries.definitionCN: 不服从的；违抗的，比 naughty 更正式、责备更重。

entries.definition: Impolite or offensive, covering the adult sense of naughty jokes and words.
entries.definitionCN: 粗鲁的；冒犯的，涵盖 naughty 表示下流玩笑的成人用法。

normalIntro.en: The family is small and grows straight out of the old noun naught, so the history itself is the best memory hook.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词族很小，直接从古名词 naught 长出，词史本身就是最好的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Naughty begins with naught, nothing, so a naughty child is one who does no good at that moment.
normal.cn: naughty 开头就是 naught（无），所以 naughty 的孩子就是那一刻「没干好事」的孩子。

normal.en: Naught and aught are a pair: naught means nothing and aught means anything, and naughty keeps the negative side.
normal.cn: naught 与 aught 成对：前者是「无」，后者是「有」，naughty 继承的是否定的一边。

normal.en: Naughtily and naughtiness are plain suffix jobs, so the family is easy to keep straight.
normal.cn: naughtily 与 naughtiness 都只是普通后缀加工，词族一目了然。

normal.en: Parents say naughty but rarely wicked, because the blame is meant to be mild and loving.
normal.cn: 家长说 naughty 而很少说 wicked，因为这份责备本意是轻微且带着爱的。

normal.en: A naughty joke is an adult borrowing of the same word: what children should not say, grown-ups giggle at.
normal.cn: naughty joke 是同一个词的成人挪用：孩子不该说的话，大人听了偷笑。

abstract.en: A word that once meant worthless ended up scolding children, showing how harsh words wear soft with daily use.
abstract.cn: 一个曾表示「毫无价值」的词最后用来数落孩子，可见严厉的词在日常使用中会磨得温和。

abstract.en: The crumbs behind the sofa are the whole word: a small wrong that everyone forgives.
abstract.cn: 沙发后面的饼干渣就是这个词的全部：一桩人人都肯原谅的小错。

abstract.en: To call a pleasure naughty is to enjoy the tiny guilt as part of the treat.
abstract.cn: 称一份享受为 naughty，是把那一点点罪恶感当作甜头的佐料。

examples.en: The naughty boy hid behind the door to scare his sister.
examples.cn: 这个调皮的男孩躲在门后吓唬妹妹。

examples.en: Eating dessert before dinner felt very naughty to her.
examples.cn: 在正餐前先吃甜点，她觉得这样真是不够乖。

examples.en: The film had a few naughty jokes but nothing cruel.
examples.cn: 这部电影里有几个下流的笑话，但并不刻薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹偷」——闹着偷吃饼干的小孩，被大人骂一声 naughty，记住是「调皮的」。

root: 古英语名词 naught（无、恶）+ 形容词词尾 -y 构成，源流清楚；naught 一般重构为日耳曼语的否定复合词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is falling short of good; from it come mild mischief in children and rude humour in adults.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「不及于善」；由此长出孩子的轻微淘气，再滑向成人的下流幽默。

intro.cn: 这个词族建立在古名词 naught 之上，配以普通的英语词尾，每个成员都贴近「无、没干好事」的核心义。

latinIntro.en: The word is fully Germanic in origin, and no Latin cognate belongs to this family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词完全是日耳曼来源，词族里没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 附近的；邻近的；在附近；就近
definition_en: a short distance away from the place being talked about, used either before a noun or after a verb
core_image: 两户人家的院墙只隔一条窄巷，站在门口就能看见对方窗里的灯
scene: 傍晚的巷口，两棵梧桐树下摆着几张矮桌，邻居端着碗坐在门口。A nearby shop was still open, and the children ran in for sweets.

senses.title: Close to the place mentioned, before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun for a place or thing that is only a short distance from the place being talked about
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词之前，指距离所说地点不远的地方或事物
senses.example: A nearby shop was still open, and the children ran in for sweets.
senses.exampleCN: 附近一家小店还开着，孩子们跑进去买糖。
senses.why: Near came from Old English neah, close at hand, and by from Old English bi, beside; putting them together produced a word whose whole job is to sit in front of a place and shorten the distance.
senses.whyCN: near 来自古英语 neah，意为「在手边」；by 来自古英语 bi，意为「在旁边」；两者合起来，造出一个专门放在地点名词前、把距离缩短的词。

senses.title: At a short distance away, after a verb
senses.definition: used after a verb or at the end of a clause to say that something happens a short distance from the place mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 放在动词之后或句末，表示事情发生在离所说地点不远的地方
senses.example: She lives nearby and walks over most mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 她住在附近，大多数早晨都走过来。
senses.why: English often lets a compound work as an adverb without any ending, so the same two prepositions that named a place beside another place also came to describe where an action happens.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让一个复合词不带词尾就直接作副词，于是原本用来说「在一个地点旁边的另一个地点」的两个介词，也用来描述动作发生在哪里。

intro.en: Nearby is a plain English compound of two Old English words for closeness, and it has been recorded only since the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: nearby 是两个表示「接近」的古英语词合成的普通英语复合词，有记录的历史只能追溯到十八世纪。

items.en: Neah meant close at hand, and its comparative near later became an ordinary adjective for what is not far.
items.cn: neah 意为在手边，它的比较级 near 后来变成普通形容词，表示「不远的」。

items.en: Bi meant beside, near or by the side of, and it survives in by, beside and the second half of nearby.
items.cn: bi 意为在旁边、靠近，它留在 by、beside 以及 nearby 的后半截里。

items.en: Middle English already paired near with by in phrases about standing or living close to a place.
items.cn: 中古英语已在表示「站在或住在某处近旁」的短语里把 near 与 by 配在一起。

items.en: The written compound nearby appears in the eighteenth century, first in American usage, and spreads in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 写成一个词的 nearby 在十八世纪出现，最早见于美国用法，十九世纪渐渐流行。

items.en: Modern English uses it both before nouns and after verbs, so one form covers two grammatical jobs.
items.cn: 现代英语让它既用于名词之前，也用于动词之后，同一个形式承担两种语法角色。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply near plus by, two old English words for closeness that fused into one adjective and adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 near 加 by，两个表示「接近」的古英语词合并成一个形容词兼副词。

normal.en: Old English neah meant close at hand, and by came from bi, beside; nearby is those two ideas welded together.
normal.cn: 古英语 neah 意为在手边，by 来自 bi（在旁边）；nearby 就是这两个意思焊在一起。

normal.en: The compound is written as one word, unlike the phrase near by, which still appears in older texts.
normal.cn: 这个复合词写成一个词，与旧文献里仍能见到的短语 near by 不同。

normal.en: Before a noun it is an adjective: a nearby town; after a verb it is an adverb: she lives nearby.
normal.cn: 放在名词前是形容词：a nearby town；放在动词后是副词：she lives nearby。

normal.en: Nearly looks like the same word with -ly, but it means almost, not at a short distance.
normal.cn: nearly 看起来只是加了 -ly，意思却是「几乎」，而不是「在不远处」。

normal.en: Nearness is the noun made with -ness, useful when the sentence needs a subject rather than a place.
normal.cn: nearness 是用 -ness 构成的名词，句子需要一个主语而不是地点时就用它。

abstract.en: Two short words for standing beside something can do the work of a whole phrase about distance.
abstract.cn: 两个表示「站在旁边」的短词，就能顶替一整句关于距离的描述。

abstract.en: A word that only shortens distance shows how much English trusts a compound to do a preposition's job.
abstract.cn: 一个只负责缩短距离的词，说明英语多么信任复合词去承担介词的工作。

abstract.en: What is nearby is not yet reached, which is why the word always leaves a small gap open.
abstract.cn: 「附近的」东西还没有被走到，所以这个词总留着一小段没走完的距离。

examples.en: Several nearby farms lost power in the storm.
examples.cn: 附近几座农场在风暴中停了电。

examples.en: The hotel is convenient for nearby restaurants.
examples.cn: 这家旅馆去附近的餐馆很方便。

examples.en: My parents live nearby, so we see them often.
examples.cn: 我父母住在附近，所以我们常去看他们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼尔拜」——抬脚就到旁边那条街，说一声就到了；nearby 就是附近的。

root: 古英语 neah（近）与 bi（在旁）复合，十八世纪出现 nearby；属日耳曼语词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place at a short distance; the same form then splits by grammar into an adjective in front of nouns and an adverb after verbs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「距离不远的一处地方」；同一个形式随后按语法分工，成了名词前的形容词和动词后的副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two garden walls separated by a narrow lane, each house able to see the other's lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：两户院墙之间只隔一条窄巷，各家都能看见对方窗里的灯。

branches.en: a shop two doors down the lane
branches.cn: 隔两个门面的那家小店

branches.en: a village within walking distance
branches.cn: 走几步就到的村子

branches.en: a lane where both walls can see one lamp
branches.cn: 两面墙都看得见同一盏灯的窄巷

branches.en: a neighbour walking over with a bowl
branches.cn: 端着一只碗走过来的邻居

branches.en: a short walk taken most mornings
branches.cn: 大多数早晨都要走的一小段路

intro.en: The word is built from an Old English adjective of closeness, an Old English preposition of position, and the English endings that grew around them.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语中表示「接近」的形容词、表示位置的介词，以及围着它们长出的英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Near and by are Germanic words, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for the compound.
latinIntro.cn: near 与 by 都是日耳曼语词，这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 几乎；差不多；将近；密切地
definition_en: not quite, but very close to being true or to happening; also used before amounts to mean a little less than the figure
core_image: 车门在眼前缓缓合上，脚尖离踏板只差半步
scene: 雨刚停，站台上的人陆续散去，广播已经在报最后一班车。I nearly missed the last train because the lift was slow.
sceneCN: 这里是「几乎、差一点」（第 1 个义项：接近但未达到）；句意为电梯太慢，我差一点错过末班车。图中可辨识物件：站台、广播、湿地面、车门。

pos.zh: 几乎；差不多；将近；密切地

derivatives.zh: nearly 的词根，义为「近的；接近的」
由 near 加 -ness 构成，义为「接近；临近」，与 nearly 同族

senses.title: Almost, but not completely
senses.definition: not quite true or not quite done, though very close to it
senses.definitionCN: 非常接近，但还没有完全达到或完成
senses.example: I nearly missed the last train because the lift was slow.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯太慢，我差一点错过末班车。
senses.why: Near began as a word for physical closeness, and the ending -ly first meant in a close manner; spoken English then stretched that short gap from space into degree, so a thing that is close to happening becomes nearly happening.
senses.whyCN: near 原本表示空间上的接近，词尾 -ly 最初意为「以接近的方式」；口语把这个小缝隙从空间拉到位次，于是「接近发生」的事就成了「几乎发生」。

senses.title: Very close to a stated amount or time
senses.titleCN: 将近；差不多（数量或时间）
senses.definition: used before figures and periods to say that the real amount is a little below the one named
senses.definitionCN: 放在数字与时间段之前，表示实际数量略低于所说的那个数
senses.example: Nearly a thousand people came to the opening.
senses.exampleCN: 将近一千人参加了开幕式。
senses.why: Measuring a short distance and measuring a small shortfall use the same picture, so the word that once said two places are close now says a total is close to a round figure.
senses.whyCN: 量一小段距离与量一小点差额用的是同一幅画面，于是那个原本说「两地相近」的词，现在说「总数接近某个整数」。

senses.title: Closely, in family connections
senses.titleCN: 密切地；亲近地（指亲属关系）
senses.definition: used with related or connected to mean closely, chiefly in older or careful English
senses.definitionCN: 与 related 等词连用表示「关系密切」，多见于较旧或较正式的英语
senses.example: The two families were nearly related by marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个家庭因婚姻而关系很近。
senses.why: The older sense of the adverb was simply closely, and kinship is where that sense survives; the everyday sense moved away to almost, leaving this use behind like a fossil.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词较早的意思就是「紧密地」，亲属关系正是这层意思的留存处；日常义漂向「几乎」，把这一用法像化石一样留在了原地。

intro.en: Nearly is near plus the old adverb ending, and its meaning drifted from closely to almost while one formal use kept the older sense.
intro.cn: nearly 是 near 加旧副词词尾，词义从「紧密地」漂到「几乎」，只有一种正式用法保留了旧义。

items.en: Neah meant close at hand, and its comparative gave English the form near that nearly is built on.
items.cn: neah 意为在手边，它的比较级给英语提供了 near 这个形式，nearly 就建在它上面。

items.en: The ending -lice meant in the manner of, and it is the ancestor of the modern -ly in nearly and other adverbs.
items.cn: -lice 意为「以……的方式」，是现代副词词尾 -ly 的前身，nearly 等词都用它。

items.en: Middle English ner meant both near and closely, and the new adverb nerliche carried the sense of closely, carefully.
items.cn: 中古英语 ner 兼有「近」与「紧密」两义，新的副词 nerliche 表示「紧密地、仔细地」。

items.en: The adverb is recorded in the sixteenth century; by the seventeenth the sense almost is common in speech and in print.
items.cn: 这个副词在十六世纪见于记录；到十七世纪，「几乎」义已在口语与书面语中常见。

items.en: Modern English keeps almost as the main sense, adds the counting use before numbers, and retains closely only in phrases about kinship.
items.cn: 现代英语以「几乎」为主义，又添上数字前的计量用法，只在与亲属关系有关的短语里保留「密切地」。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the root and the forms built directly on it; the near-meaning group holds other adverbs that stop just short of a fact.
note.cn: 形近组收词根以及直接建在词根上的形式；近义组收其他表示「差一点、差不多」的副词。

entries.definition: Not far away, in space, time or degree.
entries.definitionCN: 空间、时间或程度上不远的。

entries.definition: The quality of being close, made with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ness 构成的「接近、临近」这一性质。

entries.definition: The comparative of near, for a smaller distance.
entries.definitionCN: near 的比较级，表示更近的距离。

entries.definition: The superlative of near, for the smallest distance.
entries.definitionCN: near 的最高级，表示最近的距离。

entries.definition: Very close to, and often interchangeable with nearly before a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 非常接近，在动词前常可与 nearly 互换。

entries.definition: In effect, though not strictly true; stronger in speech than nearly.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上差不多，口语中语气比 nearly 更强。

entries.definition: Almost entirely, used of conditions rather than of counted things.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎完全，多用于状态而非可数之物。

entries.definition: About, allowing for a margin on either side rather than falling short.
entries.definitionCN: 大约，允许上下浮动，而不专指不足。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic root for closeness with an old adverb ending, and its main sense has slid from manner into degree.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语「接近」词根加旧副词词尾，主义从「方式」滑到了「程度」。

normal.en: Near means close, and -ly once meant in that manner, so nearly first described how something was done, not how complete it was.
normal.cn: near 意为近，-ly 原表示「以那种方式」，所以 nearly 最初描述的是做法，而不是完成程度。

normal.en: Before a verb, nearly and almost usually exchange freely: I nearly fell, I almost fell.
normal.cn: 在动词前，nearly 与 almost 通常可以互换：I nearly fell 与 I almost fell 意思相同。

normal.en: Before a number, nearly means a little below it; about or approximately allows the figure to be above as well.
normal.cn: 在数字前，nearly 表示略低于该数；about 或 approximately 则允许高于该数。

normal.en: Not nearly is a fixed phrase of strong denial: the job is not nearly finished means it is far from finished.
normal.cn: not nearly 是语气很强的固定说法：「the job is not nearly finished」意为「离完成还差得远」。

normal.en: Nearly related keeps the old sense of closely, which is why it sounds formal beside the everyday almost.
normal.cn: nearly related 保留了「密切」的旧义，所以它放在日常的 almost 旁边会显得正式。

abstract.en: A closing door measured in half steps shows how English turns a gap in space into a gap in degree.
abstract.cn: 用半步来量的合上的车门，说明英语怎样把空间里的缝隙变成程度上的缝隙。

abstract.en: The same word can fall just short of a train and just short of a thousand, because counting is only measuring with numbers.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以差一点赶上车，也可以差一点到一千，因为计数不过是拿数字来量。

abstract.en: A fossil sense survives in family talk, reminding us that nearly once meant tightly, not almost.
abstract.cn: 一个化石般的旧义活在亲属称谓里，提醒人 nearly 曾经意为「紧紧地」，而不是「几乎」。

examples.en: The bottle is nearly empty; we need another.
examples.cn: 瓶子快空了，我们得再拿一瓶。

examples.en: She has worked here for nearly twenty years.
examples.cn: 她在这里工作了将近二十年。

examples.en: It was nearly midnight when the phone rang.
examples.cn: 电话响的时候已将近午夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼尔利」——差一步就到「near」，可惜还没到；nearly 就是几乎、差一点。

root: 古英语 neah（近）的比较级 near，加副词词尾 -lice（现代 -ly）构成；属日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small remaining gap; it can be a gap before an event, a gap below a number, or the old gap of close kinship.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「剩下的一小段差距」；它可以是事件之前的差距、数字以下的差距，也可以是旧义里亲属之间的贴近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a train door sliding shut while one foot is still half a step from the step.
core.cn: 核心意象：车门正在合上，一只脚离踏板还差半步。

branches.en: a hand reaching a door as it closes
branches.cn: 车门合上时伸过去的手

branches.en: a platform emptying after the last announcement
branches.cn: 最后一次广播后渐渐空去的站台

branches.en: a hall filled just short of a thousand
branches.cn: 坐得差一点满一千人的大厅

branches.en: a guest list counted twice at a wedding
branches.cn: 婚礼上数了两遍的宾客名单

branches.en: two families joined by one marriage
branches.cn: 因一桩婚姻连在一起的两家人

intro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective of closeness, an Old English adverb ending, and the modern shapes of both.
intro.cn: 这个词由日耳曼语表示「接近」的形容词、一个古英语副词词尾，以及两者在现代的形式构成。

latinIntro.en: Nearly belongs to the Germanic family of near, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: nearly 属于 near 这一日耳曼语词族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
